name: Lepide Design System
setup: import "@lepide/ds-css" once; load Manrope 400–800 and Geist Mono 400/500 from Google Fonts; wrap the app in <LepideProvider link={RouterLink}> (optional), <ThemeProvider>, <ToastProvider> and render <TooltipHost /> once.

components.title: Avatar
components.summary: Round initials avatar with a tint picked from the name, and Person, an avatar plus name and optional detail on one line.

guidance.When to use:
- `Person` in table cells, detail panels and activity lists to show who did something ("CORP\\jsmith · Domain Admins").
- `Avatar` on its own where only the initials fit, for example a stack of owners or a narrow column.
guidance.When not to use:
- The signed-in user's account button in the sidebar or top bar: those use their own ink avatars (`.lf-dock__avatar`, `.hometop__avatar`, `.umenu__av`).
- Non-person objects (servers, groups, files): use an `Icon` instead.
- Photos: `Avatar` only renders initials.
guidance.Anatomy:
**Avatar** (`.fx-av`)
1. Circle, 28 × 28 by default, 700 10.5/1 initials.
2. Tint: one of five, picked by a hash of `name`, so the same name always gets the same tint — `--brand-100` / `--brand` (`.fx-av`), `#e4efe9` / `#1d7a55` (`--1`), `#f6e7df` / `#a4552c` (`--2`), `#ece8f6` / `#5a4a9a` (`--3`), `#e6edf1` / `#3e6276` (`--4`).
3. Initials: up to two letters. Everything up to the last `\` or `@` is dropped (`CORP\john.smith` → `john.smith`), the rest is split on `.`, `_`, space and `-`, and the first letters of the first two words are used, upper-cased: "Ann Lee" → AL, `CORP\john.smith` → JS, `CORP\jsmith` → J. An empty name shows `?`.
4. Native tooltip: `title` is the full name.

**Person** (`.fx-who`): inline flex row, 10 px gap — a 28 px `Avatar`, then `.fx-name` (600, `--ink`, single line with ellipsis). `sub` follows the name as ` · sub` in 500 `--ink-4`.

Initials come from `initialsOf`: it drops a `DOMAIN\` prefix and an `@domain` suffix, then takes the first letters of the first two words split on `.`, `_`, `-` or spaces ("Ann Lee", "ann.lee@corp.com" and "CORP\ann.lee" all give "AL"; "CORP\jsmith" gives "J").
guidance.Variants and sizes: `size` sets the width and height in px (default 28). It does not scale the 10.5 px initials, so keep sizes between 24 and 36. `Person` always uses 28.
guidance.States: None.
guidance.Accessibility:
- The avatar is a `<span>` whose text is the initials; screen readers read the letters. In `Person` the full name follows, so the initials are redundant but harmless.
- On its own, `Avatar` exposes the full name only through `title`, which is not reliably announced. Put the name in visible text or an adjacent `sr-only` span.
- Tints are decoration; they carry no meaning.
guidance.Do and don't:
| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| `Person` in table cells, with the group or role in `sub` | An initials avatar with no name anywhere |
| Pass a display name, `DOMAIN\user` or an email | Build initials yourself and pass them as `name` |
| Keep the 28 px default in tables | Large avatars with tiny initials |
| Let the hash pick the tint | Map tints to roles or risk |
guidance.Example: ```tsx import { Person, Avatar } from '@lepide/ds-react'; Owners: Ann Lee, Raj Patel ``` Plain HTML (with `@lepide/ds-css`): ```html J CORP\jsmith · Domain Admins ```

components.title: Banner
components.summary: Inline tinted message strip with a tone icon, text, an optional action and an optional dismiss button — for persistent notices inside a page, card or dialog.

guidance.When to use:
- A notice that stays visible while the user works with the content around it: "Licence expires in 7 days", "This report includes only the last 90 days", "2 agents are offline".
- A form or dialog-level error or warning above the fields ("Couldn't connect to the SMTP server").
- A success message that should persist on the page (for example after an import, with a link to the results).
guidance.When not to use:
- Short-lived confirmation of an action: use a toast (`useToast`).
- A field-level validation message: use the field's `error`.
- An empty or failed section with nothing else to show: use `EmptyState`.
- Marketing or promotional content.
guidance.Anatomy:
1. Container (`.banner`): flex row, items aligned to the top, 10 px gap, padding 10 14, radius 14 (`--r-md`), 500 13/19 `--ink-2` text, tone background.
2. Tone icon: 16 px, 2 px top offset, tone colour. `info` → `info`, `success` → `check`, `warning` and `error` → `alert`.
3. Message (`children`) in a `.grow` block that takes the remaining width; `<b>` inside it is `--ink`.
4. Optional action (`action`): any node after the message, usually a small `Button` or a `.lf-link`.
5. Optional dismiss button (when `onClose` is set): 26 × 26 icon button (`.lf-btn--icon.banner__x`) with a 14 px `x`, `aria-label="Dismiss"`.
guidance.Variants and sizes:
| Tone | Background | Icon colour | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| `info` (default) | `--brand-50` | `--brand-ink` | `status` |
| `success` | `--success-bg` | `--success-text` | `status` |
| `warning` | `--warning-bg` | `--warning-text` | `alert` |
| `error` | `--danger-bg` | `--danger-text` | `alert` |

The text stays `--ink-2` in every tone; only the background and icon change. One size.
guidance.States:
| State | Change |
|---|---|
| Dismiss button hover | `--surface-3` fill, icon turns `--ink` (icon button hover) |
| Dismiss button focus | 2 px brand focus outline |

The component does not hide itself: `onClose` is called and you remove the banner from your state.
guidance.Accessibility:
- `warning` and `error` use `role="alert"` and are announced immediately when they appear; `info` and `success` use `role="status"` (polite). Don't mount several alert banners at once.
- The message must make sense without the colour or icon: start with what happened ("Couldn't connect…", "Licence expires…").
- The dismiss button is named "Dismiss"; with `TooltipHost` mounted it shows that name as a tooltip.
- After dismissing, move focus somewhere sensible if the banner had focus.
guidance.Do and don't:
| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| One banner per area, at the top of the content it is about | A stack of banners |
| Plain sentences with the key fact in `<b>` | All-bold or all-caps text |
| `warning` / `error` only for real problems | `error` tone for neutral information |
| A clear action: "Renew licence", "View agents" | "Click here" |
guidance.Example:
```tsx import { Banner, Button } from '@lepide/ds-react'; Renew licence} onClose={() => setShowLicence(false)} > Your licence expires on 14 November 2026. Auditing stops after that date. This report shows changes from the last 90 days. ``` Plain HTML (with `@lepide/ds-css`): ```html
Couldn't connect to the SMTP server.
```

components.title: Button
components.summary: Pill-shaped buttons for actions. One blue primary per view, rightmost; everything else secondary, ghost or danger.

exports.name: Button
exports.description: Lepide Design System pill button (03 § 1). One primary per screen or dialog, rightmost.

props.name: dot
props.description: Brand dot at the top right (e.g. "Modify filters" while filters are applied).

exports.name: IconButton
exports.description: Icon-only button (03 § 2).

props.name: label
props.description: Required accessible name; the floating tooltip shows it.

guidance.When to use:
- `Button` for any action the user starts: save, create, export, open a dialog, apply a filter.
- `variant="primary"` for the single main action of a page, dialog, drawer or wizard step.
- `IconButton` for compact, repeated or toolbar actions where an icon is unambiguous (close, refresh, more, row actions).
guidance.When not to use:
- Navigation to another page: use a link (`<a className="lf-link">` or your router link), not a button.
- Choosing one of several options: use `Segmented`, `RadioGroup` or `Dropdown`.
- More than one primary in the same view — demote the others to `secondary`.
- A black or ink-filled button: the design has none.
guidance.Anatomy:
1. Pill container: height 38 (`--btn-h`), padding 0 16, radius 999, 1 px border, `--sh-xs`.
2. Optional leading icon, 16 px, 8 px gap (replaced by a 15 px spinner while `loading`).
3. Label: 600 13/1 Manrope, sentence case, a verb ("Create report", "Save").
4. Optional trailing icon (`iconEnd`), 14 px — e.g. a chevron for buttons that open a menu.
5. Optional brand dot (`dot`): 8 px, top-right, 2 px white ring — "this has something applied".

`IconButton`: 34 × 34 round, transparent, 16 px ink-3 icon; `bordered` adds a 1 px border, white fill and `--sh-xs` (class `is-bordered`, so plain HTML can use it too).
guidance.Variants and sizes:
| Variant | Look | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `secondary` (default) | White, 1 px `--border`, ink text | Every non-primary action |
| `primary` | `--sel-fill` blue gradient, `--brand-600` border, white text, `--sh-brand` glow | The one main action, rightmost |
| `ghost` | Secondary with 500-weight ink-2 text (`.lf-pill`) | Low-emphasis actions in toolbars |
| `danger` | Secondary with danger text and red-tinted border | Destructive action that still asks for confirmation |
| `danger-solid` | `--danger` fill, white text, red glow | Confirm button inside a destructive `ConfirmDialog` only |

Sizes: `sm` 32 tall, padding 0 13, 12.5 px · `md` 38 (default) · `lg` 44 tall, padding 0 20, 14 px. `block` stretches to full width.
guidance.States:
| State | Change |
|---|---|
| Hover | Secondary: `--border-2`, `--surface-2`, `--sh-sm`. Primary: darker gradient, `--brand-700` border, bigger glow; its icon nudges 1 px right |
| Pressed | `scale(.97)` for 80 ms; primary turns `--brand-700` |
| Focus | 2 px brand outline (`--focus-outline`), offset 2 px |
| Disabled | Opacity .45, no shadow, not clickable |
| Loading | Spinner replaces the leading icon, button disabled, `aria-busy="true"` |
| Icon button hover | `--surface-3` fill, icon turns ink; `danger` turns it red |
guidance.Accessibility:
- Renders a real `<button type="button">` (pass `type="submit"` inside forms).
- `IconButton` requires `label`: it becomes `aria-label` and the tooltip text (`TooltipHost` must be mounted once).
- Loading sets `aria-busy` and disables the button so it can't be pressed twice.
- Never rely on colour alone for danger — the label says what happens ("Delete 3 reports").
guidance.Do and don't:
| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| One primary per view, placed last (rightmost) | Two primaries side by side |
| Verb labels in sentence case: "Create dashboard" | "OK", "Submit", Title Case Labels |
| `danger-solid` only as the confirm step of a destructive action | A red solid button as the first click |
| `loading` while an async action runs | Disable the button with no feedback |
| `IconButton` with a clear `label` | Icon-only buttons without a tooltip |
guidance.Example:
```tsx import { Button, IconButton } from '@lepide/ds-react';
``` Plain HTML (with `@lepide/ds-css`): ```html ```

components.title: Card
components.summary: White rounded containers. Card for content panels, SetCard for settings sections with head, body and footer, KeyValues for read-only field tiles.

exports.name: Card
exports.description: White card. `actions` (small icon buttons, a menu) sit at the right of the title — e.g. dashboard panel tools.

exports.name: SetCard
exports.description: Settings content card: head (title, description, actions), body, optional footer.

exports.name: KeyValues

guidance.When to use:
- `Card`: any content block on a page — a chart panel, a table, a list, a summary. Cards float on the washed canvas.
- `SetCard`: one section of a settings or configuration page, with a title, a description, optional header actions, a body of fields and an optional footer of buttons.
- `KeyValues`: read-only details of a record (detail panels, review steps of a wizard, "About this agent").
guidance.When not to use:
- Grouping a few fields inside a form: use spacing or a `.section-label`, not a nested card.
- Cards inside cards: use `KeyValues` tiles or plain sections instead.
- KPI numbers: use `KpiCard`.
- Editable values: `KeyValues` is read-only; use form fields.

| Variant | How | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `flush` | `<Card flush>` | Padding 0 (inline style) — for tables or charts that run to the card edge |
| `actions` | `<Card title="…" actions={<IconButton …/>}>` | Small tools at the right of the title (`.lf-card__head` + `.lf-card__actions`) — e.g. a dashboard panel's refresh and menu |

- `Card` and `SetCard` render `<section>`; their titles are `<h3>`. Keep the heading order of the page: the page title is the `<h2>` from `PageHeader`.

- `KeyValues` renders a real `<dl>` with `<dt>` / `<dd>` pairs, so label and value are announced together.
- The em dash for empty values is read as "dash"; if that matters, pass explicit text such as "Not set".

| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| White cards with 16 px gaps (`--card-gap`) on the canvas | Full-width bordered boxes or heavy dividers |
| `flush` for a table that fills the card | Add padding around a table inside a padded card |
| `SetCard` footer with the save button rightmost | Save buttons scattered in the body |
| `KeyValues` for read-only record details | Disabled inputs to show read-only values |
| `lf-card--lift` only when the whole card is a link | Hover lift on static cards |

components.title: Chart
components.summary: Highcharts-based charts in the Lepide Design System theme — one Chart component with a kind per product chart type (columns, stacked, bars, areas, lines, donuts, gauges, rings, bubbles), plus a borderless Sparkline. Imported from '@lepide/ds-react/charts'.

exports.name: Chart
exports.description:
Lepide Design System chart for a product chart kind. `onSelect(label)` adds click-through from a segment/category.
Height defaults: 270 in a panel, 300 in a wide panel.

exports.name: Sparkline
exports.description: KPI sparkline (56 px area, gradient 22 %→0 %).

guidance.When to use:
- Any chart on a dashboard, report summary or record page. Pick the `kind` from the table below by the question the chart answers.
- `Sparkline` for a tiny trend with no axes — normally inside `KpiCard` (`spark` prop), occasionally in a table cell or list row.

Set-up:
- Import from the separate entry: `import { Chart, Sparkline } from '@lepide/ds-react/charts'`. The main `@lepide/ds-react` entry does not include charts, so apps without charts don't load Highcharts.
- Install the peer dependency `highcharts` `^13.1.1` (optional peer of `@lepide/ds-react`). The component loads `highcharts-more` and `solid-gauge` itself. **Highcharts is commercial software: a Highcharts licence is required before it ships in a product.**
guidance.When not to use:
- Exact values the user will read or copy: use a `DataTable` (or show both).
- One number: use `KpiCard`.
- More than 6 series or about 8 donut slices: the palette repeats after 6 colours; group the tail into "Other" or use a table.
- No data: show an `EmptyState` in the panel instead of an empty chart.
guidance.Anatomy:
`Chart` renders `<figure class="atl-chart">` containing:
1. The Highcharts plot, `height` px tall (default 270; use 300 in a wide panel). No chart title — the card header (`.lf-card__title`) is the title. Transparent background, Manrope, no credits.
2. Axes: labels 11 px `--chart-text` (`#666b74`), no axis lines or ticks, horizontal grid `--chart-grid` (`#eceef1`). Category labels wrap under their column instead of tilting; `dd-mm-yyyy` (or `/`) labels are shortened to `20 Nov`.
3. Legend: top-left, 600 12 px `#4a4f58`, 8 px round symbols, 22 px between items. Shown when there is more than one series, and always for donuts and rings (bottom centre there). `options.legend` forces it on or off.
4. Tooltip `.atl-tip`: white card, 1 px `--border`, radius 12, `--sh-md`; head row on `--surface-2` with the category in 700 ink; rows of an 8 px colour dot, series name and value (700, tabular). Multi-series kinds share one tooltip per category. Donut, gauge and ring kinds have no tooltip — the centre label shows the hovered part.
5. Centre label `.atl-chart__center` (donuts, speedometer, rings): value 600 28 px ink over a 500 12 px `--ink-3` caption. `.is-big` (speedometer): 36 px value, caption in the band colour. `.is-small` (rings): 19 px value, 80 px max width.
6. A visually hidden data table (`.sr-only`) with `title` as its caption.

Series colours follow `--c1`…`--c6`: `#1c4599`, `#ee8a5f`, `#b8c8f0`, `#4f72c4`, `#f5c39e`, `#8aa3dc`. Any `color` in the data may be a hex value or a product colour name written as `var(--chart-red)`, `var(--dch-orange)` etc. (mapped to Lepide Design System values); anything else, including `var(--c2)`, falls back to the palette by position.

`Sparkline`: `<div class="atl-chart">`, an area spline with a 2 px line and a 22 % → 0 % fill gradient, no axes, legend or grid; default 56 px tall, colour `#1c4599`; hover shows a "Value" tooltip.
guidance.Variants and sizes:
Every `ChartKind`, its `data` shape and when to use it:

| `kind` | `data` | Use for | Look |
|---|---|---|---|
| `columns` | `{ labels: string[], values: number[], colors?: string[], name? }` | Comparing a few categories (counts by type, by server) | Vertical columns, one palette colour per column, radius 8 on top, max 64 px wide |
| `dateColumns` | `{ labels: string[] (dates), values: number[], color?, name? }` | A count per day or week | One colour, radius 4, narrower gaps |
| `stacked` | `{ cats \| labels: string[], series: { name, values: number[], color? }[] }` | Totals per category split into parts (events by outcome per day) | Stacked columns, radius 7 on the top of each stack. `options.stacked: false` draws them side by side |
| `pairedBars` | `{ rows: string[], series: { name, values: number[], color? }[] }` | Ranking long category names, comparing 2–3 measures per row (top users: reads vs writes) | Horizontal bars, radius 5, 2 px white separators, labels truncated at 90 px |
| `areaBars` | `{ bars: number[], line: number[], labels: string[], markers?: number[], barName?, lineName? }` | Volume per period with a trend over it | Pale blue gradient columns under a 3 px `#1c4599` spline with a soft shadow and an 18 % → 0 % wash. Only bars whose index is in `markers` get an axis label: `markers[k]` is labelled `labels[k]`. Value axis 0 to the next multiple of 25, 4 dashed intervals |
| `multiArea` | `{ labels: string[], series: { name, values: number[], color?, legendColor? }[] }` | Trends of 1–4 measures over time where volume matters | 2.5 px splines with a 28 % → 2 % fill; dashed `#c9cfd8` crosshair. Values beyond `labels.length` are dropped |
| `line` | same as `multiArea` | Trends over time where only the shape matters, or many overlapping series | 2.5 px splines, no fill |
| `donut` | `{ segments: { label, value, color? }[], value?, caption?, startAngle?, showValues? }` | Share of a whole, 2–6 parts | 72 % hole, 3 px white borders; centre shows `value` (or the sum) and `caption` (default "Total") |
| `calloutDonut` | same as `donut` | Share of a whole where percentages must be visible | Donut with white percentage labels on the slices (`showValues` defaults to `true`) |
| `gaugeDonut` | same as `donut` | Product "gauge donut" screens | Drawn exactly like `donut` |
| `donut3d` | same as `donut` | Product "3D donut" screens | Drawn flat, like `calloutDonut` with percentages always on |
| `speedometer` | `{ value: number, max?: number (100), name?, bands: { to: number, label, color? }[] }` | One score against thresholds (risk score, health) | Solid gauge from −120° to 120°, 72 % hole, round caps, `--chart-track` background. The band is the first with `value <= to`; the arc is a gradient from the band colour; centre shows the rounded value and the band label in its colour |
| `rings` | `{ rings: { label, value: number (0–100), color? }[] }` | 2–4 percentages side by side (coverage, completion) | Concentric 360° solid gauges down to a 38 % hole on `--chart-track`; centre shows the first ring, or the hovered one |
| `bubbles` | `{ points: { label, x, y, size, color? }[] }` | Three measures per item (count, duration, impact) | Bubbles 12–52 px, opacity .78, 1.5 px white borders; points with the same `label` form one series; tooltip lists x, y and size |

`ChartOptions` (`options` prop):
| Field | Effect |
|---|---|
| `y: { min, max, ticks, format }` | Fixed value axis; `ticks` is the number of intervals between `min` and `max`; `format(v)` formats the labels |
| `legend` | Force the legend on (`true`) or off (`false`) |
| `markers` | Always show point markers on lines and areas (default: only on hover) |
| `stacked` | `stacked` kind only: `false` draws the series side by side |
| `onPoint(series, point)` | Click on any point, with series and point index |
| `raw` | Highcharts options merged last — a last resort |
guidance.States:
| State | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Load | 800 ms quartic ease-out: columns grow, lines draw, slices sweep |
| Data change | The chart updates in place and animates. It only rebuilds when `kind`, `data`, `height` or `options` change in content (new object literals with the same values don't re-render) |
| Hover, columns and bars | Hovered column widens 14 % and lifts on a blue drop shadow; others fade to 32 %; a 5 % blue band marks the category |
| Hover, lines and areas | Dashed crosshair; the point becomes a 6 px dot with a white ring and a halo |
| Hover, donut | The slice slides out 9 px, others fade to 40 %, the centre swaps to the slice's value and "name · N%" in its colour |
| Hover, rings and gauges | The ring brightens, others fade, the centre shows that ring |
| Hover, bubbles | The bubble grows 10 % on a shadow, others fade |
| Clickable | `onSelect(label, index)` or `options.onPoint` give every point a pointer cursor. `label` is the slice name (donuts), the ring or series name (rings, speedometer — `index` is then the series index), else the category or series name |
| Reduced motion | No load or hover animation, no slice pop-out; state changes still show |
guidance.Accessibility:
- Highcharts' own accessibility module is turned off. Instead every `Chart` renders a visually hidden `<table>` captioned with `title`: one row per category, slice, ring or point with its values (e.g. "Mon — Success 120, Failed 8"). For `areaBars` the rows are "Point 1…n" with "bar / line" values.
- `title` also becomes the figure's `aria-label`. Always pass it, matching the visible card heading.
- The centre label is `aria-hidden` (its content is in the table).
- Never encode meaning in colour alone: legends name every series, and the tooltip and table give the numbers.
- `Sparkline` has no text alternative; it is decoration next to a number (in `KpiCard` the value and delta carry the meaning).
guidance.Do and don't:
| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Put the chart in a card whose header is the title; pass the same text as `title` | Add a title inside the chart |
| Choose the kind by the question: share → `donut`, trend → `multiArea`/`line`, ranking → `pairedBars` | Donuts for trends, or lines for unordered categories |
| Use the palette order or the product colour names | Hard-code arbitrary hex colours, or `var(--c1)` (not resolved) |
| `height={300}` in wide panels, default 270 elsewhere | Very short charts that squash the axis |
| An `EmptyState` when there is no data | An empty plot with only axes |
| Get a Highcharts licence before shipping | Ship Highcharts in a product unlicensed |

components.title: Checkbox
components.summary: 16 px checkbox with a label for independent on/off choices in forms, lists and table selection; supports an indeterminate state.

exports.name: Checkbox
exports.description: Checkbox (03 § 5.2).

guidance.When to use:
- Independent yes/no choices in a form that are applied when the form is saved ("Include sub-OUs").
- A list of options where any number can be chosen.
- Row selection and "select all" headers in tables (`indeterminate` when some rows are selected).
guidance.When not to use:
- A setting that applies immediately: use `Toggle`.
- Exactly one choice from a set: use `RadioGroup`.
- Many options in a compact space: use `MultiSelect`.
guidance.Anatomy:
1. Wrapper `<label class="lf-check">`: inline flex, 10 px gap, min-height 28, 500 13/18 `--ink-2`, pointer cursor, no text selection.
2. Native `<input type="checkbox">`, visually hidden (1 × 1 px, opacity 0) but focusable.
3. Box `.lf-check__box`: 16 × 16 (`--check-size`), radius 5, 1.5 px `--border-2`, white `--surface`.
4. Tick (checked): white 4 × 8 check mark with 2 px strokes. Bar (indeterminate): white 2 px horizontal bar.
5. Optional label text.
guidance.Variants and sizes: None. One size, 16 px box.
guidance.States:
| State | Change |
|---|---|
| Hover | Box border `--ink-3` |
| Checked | Box filled `--brand`, white tick |
| Indeterminate | Box filled `--brand`, white bar. Applied only while `checked` is false |
| Focus (keyboard) | 2 px brand outline around the box (same colour as `--focus-outline`), offset 2 px |
| Disabled | Box `--surface-3` with `--border`; label `--ink-4`, not-allowed cursor |
guidance.Accessibility:
- A real checkbox inside a `<label>`: clicking the label or box toggles it; Space toggles when focused.
- With no visible `label`, pass `ariaLabel` (e.g. "Select row DC01").
- Indeterminate is set on the DOM element (`el.indeterminate`), so screen readers announce "mixed".
- Checked state is shown by the tick, not colour alone.
guidance.Do and don't:
| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Phrase labels positively: "Send a weekly summary" | Negative labels: "Don't send a summary" |
| `indeterminate` on a parent when only some children are checked | Show a parent as checked when only some children are |
| `ariaLabel` on checkboxes in table rows | Unlabelled checkboxes |
| Use for choices saved with the form | Use for instant-apply settings (that's `Toggle`) |
guidance.Example: ```tsx import { Checkbox } from '@lepide/ds-react'; ``` Plain HTML (with `@lepide/ds-css`): ```html ```

components.title: Chip
components.summary: Small read-only pills. Chip labels a thing, ToneTag shows a status with a dot and text, Counter shows a number.

exports.name: ToneTag
exports.description: StatusIndicator: a dot + text (colour never carries meaning alone).

guidance.When to use:
- `Chip`: a short, read-only label on an object — a type, a category, a role, "Beta", "AI", a licence state next to a title.
- `ToneTag`: the status of a record in a table or detail panel ("Enabled", "Failed", "Pending"). Use `toneFor(status)` to pick the tone from the status word.
- `Counter`: a number beside a toolbar or section title ("Showing 1,204 events").
guidance.When not to use:
- Anything clickable: chips are `<span>` elements with no interaction. Use `Button`, `Segmented`, or filter chips (`.fchip`) above report tables.
- Removable filter values: use the report filter chips, not `Chip`.
- Long text: chips do not wrap (`white-space: nowrap`).
- Colour as decoration: tones are for status only.
guidance.Anatomy:
**Chip** (`.lf-chip`)
1. Pill, 22 px tall (`--chip-h`), padding 0 9, `--surface-3` fill, `--ink-2` text, 600 11.5/1 (`--type-chip`).
2. Optional leading icon (`icon`), 12 px, stroke 2, 5 px gap.
3. Label.

**ToneTag** (`.fx-op`)
1. Pill, 24 px tall (`--tone-tag-h`), padding 0 10 0 8, 600 11.5/1.
2. A 6 px dot in `currentColor` (a `::before`), 6 px gap.
3. Status text.

**Counter** (`.count-chip`): pill, padding 5 9, `--surface-3` fill, 600 11.5/1 `--ink-3` text.
guidance.Variants and sizes:
`Chip` tones:

| Tone | Look | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `neutral` (default) | `--surface-3`, `--ink-2` | Plain labels |
| `brand` | `--brand-50`, `--brand` text, 1 px inset `--brand-100` ring | Highlighted labels (AI, new, current) |
| `good` | `--success-bg`, `--success-text` | Positive state |
| `warn` | `--warning-bg`, `--warning-text` | Needs attention |
| `bad` | `--danger-bg`, `--danger-text` | Error, failure, risk |
| `flat` | `--surface-3`, `--ink-3` | Low-emphasis labels |

`ToneTag` tones: `good`, `warn`, `bad` (same fills and text as the chip tones), `info` (`--brand-50`, `--brand`), `none` (default: `--surface-3`, `--ink-3`).

`toneFor(status)` maps a status label to a tone. It looks the whole label up in `STATUS_TONES` (exported, so you can read
or extend the table) and otherwise matches **whole words** in the order bad → warn → info → none → good, so
"Completed with errors" is `bad` and "Unhealthy" never reads as "healthy". A label starting with "not" that isn't in
the table is `warn`. Unknown labels are `none`. Off states are neutral, not errors.

| Tone | Statuses |
|---|---|
| `bad` | Failed, Error, Stopped, Expired, Denied, Invalid, Offline, Critical, Down, Disconnected, Unhealthy, Broken, Revoked, Blocked, Unreachable, Not running, Not connected |
| `warn` | Warning, Pending, Queued, In queue, Paused, Partial, Expiring, Degraded, Waiting, Unlicensed, Incomplete, On hold, Not configured, Not licensed, Not started |
| `info` | In progress, Indexing, Scanning, Installing, Updating, Starting, Syncing, Processing |
| `none` | Disabled, Inactive, Uninstalled, Not installed, Cancelled, Scheduled, Draft, Downloaded, Never started, Ready to install |
| `good` | Enabled, Active, Running, Success, Successful, Completed, Installed, Indexed, Online, Connected, Healthy, Valid, Licensed, Ready, Up to date |

When a screen has its own vocabulary, pass the tone explicitly or spread `STATUS_TONES` into your own map.

One size each. Inside tables a chip truncates with an ellipsis; inside KPI cards it is 24 px tall.
guidance.States: None. Chips, tone tags and counters are static.
guidance.Accessibility:
- They render plain `<span>`s; their text is read inline with the surrounding content.
- `ToneTag` never relies on colour: the status word is always shown next to the dot. Pass the full word ("Failed"), not a code.
- `Chip` accepts `title` for a native tooltip with the full text; do not put essential information only there.
- Tone text uses the `-text` colours, which meet 4.5:1 on their backgrounds.
- `Counter` shows a bare number; make sure the nearby label says what is counted.
guidance.Do and don't:
| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| `ToneTag` with `toneFor(row.status)` for status columns | A coloured chip with no status word |
| One or two words, sentence case | Sentences or Title Case Labels |
| `brand` chips sparingly, for one highlighted label | Brand chips on every row |
| Use filter chips or buttons for anything clickable | Attach `onClick` to a chip |
guidance.Example:
```tsx import { Chip, ToneTag, Counter, toneFor } from '@lepide/ds-react';

File server audit AI

{agent.status} Pending approval Events 1,204 ``` Plain HTML (with `@lepide/ds-css`): ```html Licensed Failed 1,204 ```

components.summary: Table card with title and count, sortable headers, an optional column filter row, checkbox selection, row open and row actions, client-side paging, skeleton loading and empty states, and a sticky first column.

exports.name: DataTable
exports.description: Lepide Design System table card (03 § 9): sortable headers, column filter row, pager, row actions, selection.

props.name: title
props.description: Card toolbar: title (left), count noun, extra controls (right). Omit title to hide the toolbar.

exports.name: Pager
exports.description: Lepide Design System pager (03 § 9.6).

guidance.When to use:
- Any list of records the user scans, compares, sorts, filters or acts on: users, reports, alerts, audit events, servers.
- Lists where rows open a detail view (`onRowOpen` + `Drawer` or `DetailPanel`) or carry per-row actions (`rowActions`).
- Bulk actions over many rows (`selectable="multi"`).
- `Pager` on its own under any custom list that pages the same way.
guidance.When not to use:
- A handful of label/value pairs: use `KeyValues`.
- Fewer than about 4 items with rich content: use cards (`Card`, `SetCard`).
- Server-side paging, sorting or filtering of very large sets: `DataTable` sorts, filters and pages the `rows` array in the browser. Pass it one page of data only if you also accept that its counts, sort and filters apply to that page.
- Layout grids: tables are for tabular data only.
guidance.Anatomy:
1. Card `<section class="lf-card tablecard">`: white, radius 20, no padding, overflow hidden. `flat` adds `.tablecard--flat` (no shadow, 1 px `--border-soft`).
2. Toolbar `.toolbar` (when `title` or `toolbar` is set), padding 16 20 12: title `<h3 class="lf-card__title">` (700 15/22) with a count chip `.count-chip` ("1,204 records", 600 11.5 `--ink-3` on `--surface-3`, pill) — the count is the number of rows after search and filters, worded with `noun` (singular, plural; default `['record', 'records']`). Right: your `toolbar` controls (e.g. `SearchField`, bordered 32 px icon buttons).
3. Scroll area `.tbl-wrap`: scrolls both ways; `maxHeight` caps its height so the body scrolls under a sticky header.
4. Header row: sticky, 42 tall (`--table-head-h`), `--surface-2`, 600 12/16 `--ink-3`, hairlines top and bottom, padding 0 16 (first cell 20). Sortable headers are a `.th-sort` button with a 12 px icon: `sort` when unsorted, `up` / `down` in `--brand-ink` with the header in ink when sorted.
5. Filter row `.filter-row` (when any column has `filterable`): 44 tall (`--table-filter-h`), sticky under the header. Each filterable column gets a `.filter-input` pill: 30 tall, white, 1 px `--border-soft`, 12 px search icon, placeholder "Filter", 500 12.5 text. `--brand-200` border when it has a value; `--brand-300` border plus `--ring` when focused.
6. Body rows `.lf-row`: 56 tall (`--table-row-h`), padding 0 16 (first cell 20), white, 1 px `--border-soft` between rows, 500 13/18 `--ink-2`. Cells don't wrap; long text truncates with an ellipsis and the full value is in the cell's `title`. Empty values (`''`, `null`, `undefined`) show a `--ink-4` "—". Rows fade up in a 20 ms stagger when they render.
7. First column: 600 ink, sticky on the left; a 12 px soft shadow appears on its right edge once the table is scrolled sideways (`.tbl-wrap.is-scrolled`). When the table is narrower than 760 px it stops being sticky. With `selectable="multi"` the first column is the checkbox column.
8. Checkbox column (`selectable="multi"`): 44 wide, 16 px `.lf-check` boxes; the header box selects the page.
9. Row actions column (`rowActions`): 96 wide, right-aligned `.lf-row__actions`. Put `IconButton`s in it; they are 30 px, hidden until the row is hovered or has focus inside (fade + 4 px slide), always visible on touch devices. An `IconButton` with `label="Remove"` hovers red.
10. Open column (`onRowOpen`): 52 wide, a 30 px round `arrow` (`.lf-row__open`, `--ink-4`) that takes the selected finish (`--sel-fill`, white) and slides 2 px right on row hover or when the row is selected.
11. Pager `.pager` (below the table, when not loading and `rows` is not empty): padding 12 20, top hairline. Left: total ("1,204 records"). Right: first / previous buttons, a 44 × 34 pill page input with "/ N", next / last buttons (all 34 px round, 15 px chevrons), and a "10 / page" pill that opens an upward `Menu` of `pageSizes`.

`Column<T>` fields:
| Field | Effect |
|---|---|
| `key` | Unique id; also the row property read when `value` is omitted |
| `header` | Header text, also used in the filter input's `aria-label` |
| `value(row)` | Plain value for sorting, search, column filters and the default cell |
| `render(row)` | Custom cell content (chips, links, avatars). Sorting and filtering still use `value` |
| `width`, `minWidth` | Column width in px (`minWidth` defaults to `width`) |
| `sortable` | Header becomes a sort button |
| `filterable` | Adds this column's input to the filter row |
| `mono` | Geist Mono 400 12.5/18 (`.lf-mono`) for ids, paths, hashes |
| `wrap` | Lets the cell wrap instead of truncating (`.td-wrap`) |
| `align` | `left` / `right` / `center` for header and cells (use `right` for numbers) |
guidance.Variants and sizes: `flat`: no shadow, hairline border — for a table inside another card or a drawer. Otherwise none.
guidance.States:
| State | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Sorting | Click a sortable header: ascending; click again: descending; again: ascending. Sorting never clears. Numbers compare numerically; everything else with a case-insensitive, numeric-aware string compare. `initialSort` sets the starting sort |
| Search | `search` (e.g. the value of a `SearchField`) keeps rows where any column's `value` contains the text, case-insensitive. Applied before column filters |
| Column filters | Each filter keeps rows whose column `value` contains the typed text (case-insensitive, max 200 characters). Filters combine with AND |
| Paging | `pageSizes` default `[10, 25, 50, 100]`; `defaultPageSize` default is the first size. Changing search, a filter or the page size goes back to page 1. The page input accepts a number on Enter or blur and reverts if out of range |
| Row hover | Cells turn `--surface-2`; row actions and the open arrow appear |
| Keyboard focus on a row | Cells turn `--brand-50` |
| Selected / active | Keys in `selected`, or the row matching `activeKey`, get `.is-sel`: `--brand-50` cells and a 3 px brand bar on the left of the first cell |
| Select all | The header checkbox selects every enabled row on the current page (keeping selections on other pages); it is indeterminate when some are selected; clicking it when all are on deselects that page only |
| Disabled row | `isRowDisabled(row)` sets `aria-disabled`, disables its checkbox, skips it in select-all and stops it opening or being selected. The row shows `--ink-4` text, a not-allowed cursor and no hover highlight; add a status in a cell saying why |
| Loading | `loading`: 7 skeleton rows (`.sk-rows`, 10 px shimmering pill bars), count chip reads "Loading…", pager hidden |
| Empty | `rows` is empty and `empty` is given: your `empty` content (usually an `EmptyState`) fills the body, centred on the visible width; pager hidden |
| No results | Search or filters exclude every row (or `rows` is empty with no `empty`): the `noResults` text, centred, 180 tall, `--ink-3`. Pass a specific line when you know what is listed (`noResults="No servers match your search."`) |

Selection is controlled: pass `selected` and update it from `onSelectedChange(keys)`. `selectable="single"` renders no checkboxes: clicking a row (or Enter / Space on a focused row) selects it, calling `onSelectedChange([key])`; the row gets `aria-selected="true"` and the selected style. If `onRowOpen` is also set, the same click opens it.
guidance.Accessibility:
- Real `<table>` markup with `<th>` headers. Sorted columns carry `aria-sort="ascending"` / `"descending"`; sort controls are buttons.
- With `onRowOpen`, each row is focusable (`tabIndex=0`); Enter or Space opens it. A click opens it unless it lands on a button, link, input, label, select or `.lf-toggle` inside the row, so cell controls keep working.
- Checkboxes are labelled "Select row" and "Select all rows on this page". Filter inputs are labelled "Filter {header}". The actions and open columns have visually hidden headers ("Actions", "Open").
- Pager buttons are labelled "First page", "Previous page", "Next page", "Last page"; the input is labelled "Page"; the size menu is "Rows per page".
- Selected rows add a left bar, not only a tint. Give every row-action `IconButton` a `label` (it becomes its name and tooltip).
- Skeleton rows are `aria-hidden`; the count chip says "Loading…".
guidance.Do and don't:
| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Make the first column the record's name or key | Lead with an id, date or checkbox-only column the user can't recognise |
| `value` returns plain text or a number; `render` handles the look | Return JSX from `value` (sorting and search break) |
| `align: 'right'` for numbers, `mono` for ids and paths | Centre-align text columns |
| 2–3 `IconButton` row actions; put the rest in a `Menu` | A row of five buttons in every row |
| `empty` with an `EmptyState` and a create action | A blank table body |
| Use `noun` so counts read naturally: `['user', 'users']` | "1 records" |
guidance.Example:
```tsx import { useState } from 'react'; import { DataTable, SearchField, Button, IconButton, EmptyState, ToneTag, type Column } from '@lepide/ds-react'; type User = { id: string; name: string; department: string; lastLogon: string; failed: number; status: 'Enabled' | 'Disabled' }; const columns: Column[] = [ { key: 'name', header: 'Name', sortable: true, filterable: true, minWidth: 220 }, { key: 'department', header: 'Department', sortable: true, filterable: true }, { key: 'lastLogon', header: 'Last logon', sortable: true, width: 160 }, { key: 'failed', header: 'Failed logons', sortable: true, align: 'right', width: 140 }, { key: 'status', header: 'Status', value: (u) => u.status, render: (u) => {u.status} }, ]; export function UsersTable({ users, loading, onOpen }: { users: User[]; loading: boolean; onOpen: (u: User) => void }) { const [q, setQ] = useState(''); const [selected, setSelected] = useState([]); return ( u.id} columns={columns} loading={loading} search={q} initialSort={{ key: 'failed', dir: 'desc' }} toolbar={<> } selectable="multi" selected={selected} onSelectedChange={setSelected} onRowOpen={onOpen} rowActions={(u) => onOpen(u)} />} empty={} /> ); } ``` Columns are `Column` objects: `{ key, header, value?, render?, width?, minWidth?, sortable?, filterable?, mono?, wrap?, align? }` (full definition under Props). The column title field is `header`. Plain HTML (with `@lepide/ds-css`) — the markup `DataTable` renders, for static pages. `

All users6 users

Status Actions Open
Ann Lee Active
6 users / 1
```

components.title: Date range picker
components.summary: Ghost-button popover with date presets (Today … Last Month) and a Custom Range month calendar; the change is applied only on Apply.

exports.name: DateRangePicker
exports.description: Date range picker (03 § 19): presets list, Custom Range reveals a calendar, Cancel / Apply.

exports.name: Calendar
exports.description: Month calendar selecting a start and an end.

guidance.When to use:
- `DateRangePicker` for the time range of a report, dashboard, audit log or chart — usually at the right of a page or card toolbar.
- `Calendar` on its own when you build a custom picker that needs a month grid selecting a start and end date.
guidance.When not to use:
- A single date (an expiry date, a scheduled run): `Calendar` always selects a range; use a text field with a date input instead.
- Choosing a time of day: use a `Dropdown` with `size="sm"`.
- Relative periods that are not dates ("Every Monday"): use `SelectField`.
guidance.Anatomy:
1. Trigger: `Button variant="ghost"` (pill, 38 px) with a calendar icon, the current preset name ("Last 7 Days"), or for a custom range the formatted range ("Jan 5, 2026 - Jan 12, 2026"), and a trailing chevron.
2. Popover `.pop` (`Menu`, `role="menu"`, `aria-label` from `label`, default "Date range"), at least 320 px wide, aligned to the trigger's right edge by default (`align="left"` for the left edge).
3. Body `.dp` (320 px wide, no padding).
4. Preset rows `.pop__item`: min-height 36, padding 0 10, radius 8. Rows are `role="menuitemradio"`; the selected preset has `aria-checked="true"`: `--surface-2` fill, 600 `--ink`, and a 6 px `--brand` dot at the right. Defaults: Today, Yesterday, Last 7 Days, Last 30 Days, This Month, Last Month, Custom Range.
5. Calendar `.cal` (only when "Custom Range" is selected):
   - Header `.cal__head`: previous / next month icon buttons ("Previous month", "Next month") around "January 2026" in 700 13/18 `--ink`.
   - Grid `.cal__grid`: 7 columns of 34 px, 2 px gap, weeks start on Monday (Mo … Su headers `.cal__dow`, 600 11 `--ink-3`), always 6 weeks (42 days).
   - Day `.cal__day`: 34 px round, 500 13 `--ink-2`.
6. Footer `.dp__foot`: hairline `--border-soft` above, right-aligned small `Cancel` and primary `Apply` buttons (32 px).
guidance.Variants and sizes: None. One size, 320 px panel.
guidance.States:
| State | Change |
|---|---|
| Day hover | `--surface-3` |
| Outside month (`.is-out`) | `--ink-4` |
| Today (`.is-today`) | 1 px inset `--brand` ring |
| In range (`.is-in`) | `--surface-3`, radius 8 |
| Start / end (`.is-end`) | Selected finish: `--sel-fill` blue gradient, white text, `--sel-ring`; `aria-pressed="true"` |
| Selecting (`Calendar`) | With no start, or with both ends set, a click calls `onPick(day, null)` (new start). With a start and no end, a click calls `onPick(start, day)`, or `onPick(day, start)` if the day is earlier |
| Selecting (inside `DateRangePicker`) | First click sets the start (a one-day range is shown), second click sets the end — earlier dates swap so start ≤ end. A third click starts a new range. Apply commits it |
| Draft | Preset and calendar changes are held as a draft; the trigger and `onApply` update only on Apply. Cancel, Esc or an outside click discards the draft |
guidance.Accessibility:
- The trigger gets `aria-expanded` and `aria-haspopup="menu"` from `Menu`. On open, focus moves to the first preset.
- ↓ / ↑ move between preset rows (wrapping), Home / End jump to the first / last. Tab reaches the calendar buttons and the footer. Esc or Cancel closes without applying and returns focus to the trigger; Apply also returns focus; a click outside closes without moving focus.
- Each day is a `<button>` labelled with its full date ("Jan 5, 2026") and `aria-pressed` on the start and end days. There is no arrow-key navigation inside the day grid.
- Start/end days use the selected finish plus `aria-pressed`, not colour alone.
guidance.Do and don't:
| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Put the picker at the right of the toolbar it filters | Hide the active range — the trigger always shows it |
| Keep the default presets; pass `presets` only to remove ones that don't apply | Invent presets that `rangeFor` doesn't compute (they fall back to today) |
| Re-query only in `onApply` | Re-query on every preset click |
| Keep "Custom Range" in `presets` when users need arbitrary dates | Remove it and leave no way to pick exact dates |

components.title: Drawer
components.summary: Floating side panel that slides in from the right over a scrim (Drawer), and the non-modal sticky panel beside a list (DetailPanel).

exports.name: DetailPanel
exports.description: Non-modal panel beside a list (use inside a `.with-detail` grid). Escape closes.

guidance.When to use:
- `Drawer` to show or edit the details of one item without leaving the page: a record's properties, a settings sub-form, an assistant chat, a recommendation.
- `DetailPanel` beside a table or list when the user moves between items and should keep the list visible and usable (master–detail). It does not block the page.
guidance.When not to use:
- A decision that must be answered before anything else (confirm, delete): use `ConfirmDialog`.
- A short create form that ends with a single save: a `Modal` is usually clearer.
- Navigation between sections: use a page.
- Stacking a drawer on a drawer.
guidance.Anatomy:
`Drawer` (portal into `document.body`, wrapper `.drawer lf`):
1. Container: fixed, full window, z-index 70 (`--z-drawer`, below modals at 80).
2. Scrim `.drawer__scrim`: `rgba(18,20,23,.24)` with a 2 px backdrop blur, fades in. Clicking it calls `onClose`.
3. Panel `.drawer__panel` (`<aside>`): floats 12 px (`--drawer-inset`) inside the top, right and bottom window edges; width `min(440px, 100% − 24px)` (`--drawer-w`); white; radius 26 (`--r-xl`); `--sh-lg`; enters with `slide-in` (24 px from the right, 250 ms).
4. Head `.drawer__head`, padding 22 22 14: title `<h3>` 700 18/26 −0.025em ink, optional subtitle `<small>` 500 13/18 `--ink-3`. `head` replaces the title block with your own content. Close: a bordered 34 px `.lf-btn--icon` (1 px `--border`, white, `--sh-xs`) with `aria-label="Close"`.
5. Body `.drawer__body`: fills the remaining height and scrolls; padding 6 22 20; flex column, gap 14.
6. Footer `.drawer__foot` (when `footer` or `footerNote` is passed): padding 14 22, top hairline `--border-soft`, `--surface-2`, buttons right-aligned with 8 px gap. `footerNote` sits at the left in `.lf-muted` (500 12.5/16 `--ink-3`).

`DetailPanel`: an `<aside class="lf-card detail">` with the same head, body and footer classes. It is sticky at the top of its column, max height `100dvh − 120px`, no padding of its own, enters with `slide-in`. Place it as the second child of a `.with-detail` grid: `minmax(0,1fr) 420px`, 16 px gap; under 1100 px the grid becomes one column. Its close button is also bordered.
guidance.Variants and sizes:
| `width` | Panel width | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `md` (default) | 440 | Record details, settings |
| `rec` | 480 | Recommendation / record views with more content |
| `chat` | 500 | Assistant or conversation panels |
| a number, e.g. `620` | `min(620px, 100% − 24px)` | Anything else that needs a fixed width |

Under 860 px window width the drawer becomes a bottom sheet: 8 px from the left, right and bottom, auto width, max height 86dvh, entering with `rise-in`.
guidance.States:
| State | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Closed | `open={false}` renders nothing |
| Opening | After 40 ms focus moves to the first `[data-autofocus]` element, else the first input in `.drawer__body`, else the first focusable element |
| Escape / scrim click / × | Calls `onClose` |
| Closing | Focus returns to the element that was focused when it opened |
| DetailPanel Escape | Calls `onClose` only when no modal or drawer (`[data-overlay]`) is open |
guidance.Accessibility:
- `Drawer` is `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`, with focus trapped inside (Tab and Shift+Tab wrap). It is named by its title heading (`aria-labelledby`), so any `title` works; with a custom `head` it falls back to `aria-label` from a string `title`, so pass a string title then.
- Only the top-most overlay reacts to Escape and Tab, so a `ConfirmDialog` opened from a drawer closes first.
- `DetailPanel` is a labelled `<aside>` (not a dialog): no focus trap and the page stays interactive. Move focus into it yourself if the user opened it from the keyboard.
- Both close buttons have `aria-label="Close"` and show a tooltip when `TooltipHost` is mounted.
guidance.Do and don't:
| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Keep the list visible: open details in a drawer or `DetailPanel` | Navigate away to a detail page for a quick look |
| Primary action last in `footer`; extra context in `footerNote` | Several primaries, or actions in the head |
| Highlight the open row with `DataTable` `activeKey` | Leave the user guessing which row the panel shows |
| `width="chat"` / `"rec"` for those panel types | Hand-tuned pixel widths for standard panels |
| `DetailPanel` inside `.with-detail` | `DetailPanel` floating on its own without the grid |

components.summary: Select-only combobox that replaces the native select — 46 px trigger, floating rounded panel, brand tint and check on the selected row, full keyboard support.

exports.name: Dropdown
exports.description:
Select-only combobox (WAI-ARIA APG pattern), the Lepide Design System dropdown (03 § 4).
Floating rounded panel, hover/keyboard highlight, brand tint + check on the selected row, type-to-jump,
optional search. Keyboard: ↓/↑/Enter/Space open; ↓/↑/Home/End/PageUp/PageDown move; Enter/Space pick;
Esc closes; letters jump to the next matching option.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Shown when nothing is chosen. With `clearable`, also offered as a muted first row once a value is set.

props.name: search
props.description: Search box at the top of the list: on, off, or (default) automatically past `searchFrom` options.

props.name: size
props.description: sm = 36 px compact trigger for inline use (time pickers, table cells). pill = rounded toolbar trigger.

exports.name: SelectField
exports.description: Labelled dropdown in the dialog-field style (03 § 4): the Lepide Design System <Dropdown>, not a native select.

exports.name: FloatingPop
exports.description:
Panel in a portal with fixed positioning, so dialog scroll areas can't clip it and dialog field styles
don't leak into its search box. At least as wide as the trigger; flips above it when there's no room.

guidance.When to use:
- `SelectField` for picking one value from a list inside a dialog or page form: it is a `Dropdown` wrapped in `Field` (label, note, help, error).
- `Dropdown` on its own when the label lives elsewhere (table cells, toolbars, inline time pickers) — give it `ariaLabel` or `ariaLabelledby`.
- `size="sm"` for compact inline use (tables, time pickers); `pill` for toolbar triggers.
- `FloatingPop` only when building a custom popup that must escape clipping containers (it is what `Dropdown` and `MultiSelect` render their panel into).
guidance.When not to use:
- Never use a native `<select>` — every select in the Lepide Design System is this component.
- Choosing several values: use `MultiSelect`.
- 2–4 options that should all be visible: use `RadioGroup` or `Segmented`.
- Actions ("Export", "Delete"): use `Menu` with a `Button` trigger, not a dropdown.
guidance.Anatomy:
1. Wrapper `.dd`: `position: relative`, full width.
2. Trigger `<button class="dd__trigger" role="combobox">`: height 46 (`--field-h`), radius 14 (`--field-radius`), padding 0 8 0 14, 1 px `--border`, fill `--surface-2`, 500 14/20 `--ink`.
3. Value `.dd__value`: ellipsised; placeholder state `.is-ph` in 400 `--ink-4`. With no `placeholder` the trigger shows "Select".
4. Chevron well `.dd__chev`: 28 px round, `--ink-3`, 16 px chevron.
5. Panel `.dd__pop` (via `FloatingPop`, portalled to `body`, `position: fixed`, z-index 130): at least the trigger's width (grows to fit content up to 360 px), 6 px below the trigger, flips above it when there is less room below; white, 1 px `--border`, radius 14, padding 6, two-layer soft shadow, max height 320; enters with `dd-in` (160 ms, −4 px, scale .98).
6. Optional search `.dd__search`: 38 px, radius 10 (`--r-sm`), `--surface-2`, 15 px search icon, placeholder "Search". Shown automatically when there are more than `searchFrom` (default 8) options; `search` forces it on or off.
7. List `.dd__list` (`role="listbox"`), 2 px gap between rows.
8. Option `.dd__opt` (`role="option"`): min-height 38 (`--option-h`), padding 8 10 8 12, radius 10, 500 13.5/20 `--ink-2`. Selected: `--brand-50`, `--brand-ink`, 600, 16 px check at the right.
9. "None" row `.is-none`: with `clearable` and a `placeholder`, once a value is set, the placeholder is offered as a first row in `--ink-3` with a hairline under it; picking it calls `onChange('')`.
10. Empty search result `.dd__empty`: "No matches for “…”", centred `--ink-3`.

`SelectField` sets `clearable` automatically whenever you pass a `placeholder`.
guidance.Variants and sizes:
| Variant | Look | Use |
|---|---|---|
| default | 46 px soft-filled field trigger | Forms (`SelectField`) |
| `pill` (`.dd--pill`) | 40 px pill (`--input-h`), white, `--sh-xs` | Toolbars next to pill inputs |

Sizes: `md` (default) 46 px, full width · `sm` (`.dd--sm`) 36 px (`--select-h-sm`), radius 10, 13 px text, auto width, min 72 px, 24 px chevron well.
guidance.States:
| State | Change |
|---|---|
| Hover | White fill, `--border-2` border; chevron well `--surface-3` |
| Focus (keyboard) | White, `--brand-300` border, `--ring` |
| Open | Same as focus; chevron well `--brand-50` with the chevron in `--brand-ink`, rotated 180° |
| Option active (hover or arrow keys) | `--surface-2`, `--ink`; selected and active: `--brand-100` |
| Option disabled | `--ink-4`, no hover, cannot be picked or reached with arrows |
| Invalid (`invalid`, or `error` on `SelectField`) | Danger border, white fill, `0 0 0 3px rgba(207,58,63,.12)` halo; `aria-invalid="true"` |
| Disabled | `--ink-4` text, opacity .75, not-allowed cursor, does not open |
| Reduced motion | Panel appears without the `dd-in` animation |
guidance.Accessibility:
Follows the WAI-ARIA APG select-only combobox: trigger `role="combobox"`, `aria-haspopup="listbox"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` the listbox while open, `aria-activedescendant` for the active option (on the search input instead when the search box is shown).

| Key | Closed | Open |
|---|---|---|
| ↓ / ↑ / Enter / Space | Open the list on the selected (or first enabled) option | ↓ / ↑ move to the next / previous enabled option |
| Home / End | — | First / last enabled option (not while typing in search) |
| PageDown / PageUp | — | Move 8 enabled options |
| Enter (or Space outside search) | — | Pick the active option and close |
| Esc | — | Close and return focus to the trigger |
| Tab | — | Close, focus moves on |
| Letters | Select the next option starting with the typed text | Move to it (typed characters within 700 ms combine) |

- A click outside closes the list. Mouse-downs inside the portalled panel do not count as outside clicks for a `Menu` or `Modal` the dropdown is in.
- The listbox is named by `ariaLabelledby`, else `ariaLabel`, else the placeholder. Inside `SelectField` the visible label is linked by `htmlFor`.
- Selection is never colour alone: the selected option shows a check and `aria-selected="true"`.
guidance.Do and don't:
| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| `SelectField` with a visible label in forms | A native `<select>` |
| `placeholder="All"` (with clearable) when "no value" is a valid choice | A fake "— None —" option in `options` |
| Let search turn on by itself past 8 options | Force search on a 3-option list |
| `size="sm"` in table cells and time pickers | Shrink the default trigger with custom CSS |
| `ariaLabel` on a bare `Dropdown` with no visible label | An unlabelled trigger |

components.title: EmptyState
components.summary: Centred block on a dotted field with an icon tile, a title, an optional message and an action — for empty lists, no results and load errors.

exports.name: EmptyState
exports.description: Empty, no-results or error state. Default icon: "folder" (or "alert" with tone="error"); an explicit icon always wins.

guidance.When to use:
- A list, table or panel has nothing to show yet ("No reports yet").
- A search or filter returns no results ("No events match these filters").
- A section failed to load: `tone="error"`, with a retry action.
- `compact` inside small cards and panels.
guidance.When not to use:
- While data is loading: use `SkeletonRows` or `PageLoader`.
- Inside `DataTable`, don't render it beside the table: pass it to the table's `empty` prop (shown when the table has no rows). When filters leave no rows, the table shows its own `.empty-cell` message.
- A page-level notice that sits above content that is still shown: use `Banner`.
- Transient confirmation of an action: use a toast.
guidance.Anatomy:
1. Field (`.empty`): flex column, centred, 10 px gap, padding 48 24, min-height 300, 12 px margin, radius 14 (`--r-md`), `flex: 1`. Background: 1 px dots every 18 px over `--surface-2`, edges faded with a radial mask. Text 400 14/21 `--ink-3`. 2. Icon tile (`.ring`): 56 × 56, radius 18, `--surface` fill, `--brand` icon, `--sh-md` plus a 1 px inset `--border-soft` ring, a slow pulsing `ring-out` halo (2.4 s, infinite). The icon (`icon`, default `folder`) is 24 px (`--icon-lg`). 3. Title (`title`): `

`, 700 18/26, −0.02em, `--ink`. 4. Message (`message`): `

`, max 46ch, 8 px bottom margin. 5. Action (`action`): any node, usually one `Button`.
guidance.Variants and sizes:
| Variant | Change |
|---|---|
| Default | As above |
| `compact` | Min-height 160, padding 28 20; icon tile 44 × 44 with a 20 px icon; title 600 15/22 |
| `tone="error"` | Adds `.empty--error`: icon tile `--danger-bg` fill with a `--danger-text` icon. The icon defaults to `alert` but an explicit `icon` wins. Combines with `compact` (`.empty--compact`: 44 px tile, 20 px icon, 160 px min-height) |

Dark theme: the dots are drawn in 8 % white.
guidance.States: None. The `ring-out` pulse stops after one cycle under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
guidance.Accessibility:
- Renders a plain `<div>` with an `<h4>` title. It is not a live region: if the empty or error state replaces content after a user action, announce it yourself (for example with a toast or an `aria-live` wrapper).
- The icon is decorative (`aria-hidden`).
- Pick the heading level context carefully: the title is always `<h4>`.
- The action is focusable as usual; make its label say what it does ("Create report", "Try again").
guidance.Do and don't:
| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Say what is empty and what to do next | "No data" with no explanation |
| Name what didn't match: `No reports match "finance".` (generic: `No results match your search or filters.`) | "Sorry, …", Title Case or exclamation marks |
| One action that fixes the state ("Clear filters", "Add server") | Several competing buttons |
| `tone="error"` with a "Try again" action for load failures | A red banner and an empty state for the same error |
| `compact` inside cards | A 300 px tall block in a small panel |
guidance.Example:
```tsx import { EmptyState, Button } from '@lepide/ds-react'; {rows.length === 0 && ( Clear filters} /> )} {error && ( Try again} /> )} ``` Plain HTML (with `@lepide/ds-css`): ```html

No reports yet

Create a report to start tracking changes.

```

components.title: File upload
components.summary: Dashed drop zone for choosing or dropping one file; once a file is set it turns into a file card with name, size and a remove button.

props.name: file
props.type: { name: string; size?: number | undefined; } | null

props.name: label
props.default: 'Choose a file or drop it here'

guidance.When to use:
- Importing one file in a dialog or wizard step: a CSV of users, a licence file, a certificate, a logo.
- When drag and drop from the desktop is useful, with click-to-browse as the fallback.
guidance.When not to use:
- Several files at once: `FileUpload` takes only the first file of a drop or selection.
- Entering a server path or URL: use `TextField`.
- A button-only "Import" action with no drop zone: use a `Button` that opens a hidden file input.
guidance.Anatomy:
Empty (no `file`):
1. Drop zone `.upload` (`role="button"`, `tabIndex=0`): centred column, 8 px gap, padding 24, radius 14 (`--r-md`), 1 px dashed `--border-2`, fill `--surface-2`.
2. Icon tile `.mhead__ic`, sized 40 × 40: radius 14, `--brand-50` fill, `--brand` upload icon, `--brand-100` inner hairline.
3. Label `<b>`: 600 13/18 `--ink`; default "Choose a file or drop it here".
4. Optional `rules` `<span>`: 500 12/16 `--ink-3` — accepted types and size limit.
5. Hidden `<input type="file">` with `accept`.

With a file (`file` set):
1. Card `.basecard`: flex, 12 px gap, padding 12 14, radius 14, `--surface-2`, 1 px `--border-soft`, fades up.
2. Icon `.basecard__ic`: 36 px, radius 11, white, `--brand` file icon, `--sh-xs`.
3. Text `.basecard__text`: file name 700 13.5/18 `--ink`; size in KB (one decimal) 500 12.5/17 `--ink-3`, shown when `file.size` is given.
4. Remove button (only with `onClear`): `.lf-btn.lf-btn--icon` with an × icon, `aria-label="Remove file"`.
guidance.Variants and sizes: None. The drop zone fills its container's width.
guidance.States:
| State | Change |
|---|---|
| Hover | `--brand-50` fill, `--brand-300` border |
| Dragging a file over (`.is-drag`) | Same as hover |
| Focus (keyboard) | Global 2 px brand outline (`--focus-outline`), offset 2 px |
| File chosen | Drop zone is replaced by the file card |

There is no built-in error or progress state: validate in `onFile` and show the error with `Field` (`error`) or a banner.
guidance.Accessibility:
- The drop zone is focusable and opens the file dialog on click, Enter or Space.
- Its accessible name comes from its text (label and rules), so keep the label explicit: "Choose a CSV file or drop it here".
- `accept` only filters the browser's file dialog; dropped files are not filtered — check type and size in `onFile`.
- The file input is reset after each pick, so choosing the same file again fires `onFile` again.
- The remove button has the accessible name "Remove file".
guidance.Do and don't:
| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| State accepted types and the size limit in `rules`: "CSV, up to 5 MB" | Leave the user to discover limits from an error |
| Validate in `onFile` and show a specific error under the field | Silently ignore a wrong file type |
| Pass `onClear` so the user can replace the file | Leave no way to undo a wrong pick |
| Show the file name and size once chosen | Show a generic "File uploaded" with no name |
guidance.Example:
```tsx import { Field, FileUpload } from '@lepide/ds-react'; (f.size > 5 * 1024 * 1024 ? setFileError('The file is larger than 5 MB.') : (setFileError(null), setFile(f)))} onClear={() => setFile(null)} /> ``` Plain HTML (with `@lepide/ds-css`): ```html
Choose a file or drop it here CSV, up to 5 MB
```

components.title: Icon
components.summary: Thin Lucide-style line icons (1.6 stroke, currentColor), the product module glyphs, and the Lepide mark in its white tile.

exports.name: Icon
exports.description: Lepide Design System line icon (svg.lf-i in components.css supplies stroke 1.6, round caps, currentColor).

exports.name: ModuleIcon
exports.description: Product module icon (24px outline glyph drawn with currentColor).

exports.name: BrandMark
exports.description: The Lepide mark inside its white tile.

exports.name: MARK_URL
exports.description: URL of the Lepide mark SVG (a data URL), for , favicons or a plain-HTML page.

guidance.When to use: - `Icon` for every line icon in the UI: inside buttons (via their `icon` prop), menus, chips, fields, banners, empty states and table cells. - `ModuleIcon` for the Lepide product modules (Auditor, Detect, Protect, …) in the sidebar, home tiles and Lepide AI surfaces. - `BrandMark` for the Lepide logo in the sidebar, top bar and sign-in page. - `MARK_URL` (the mark as an SVG data URL) where you need the image itself: a favicon, an `` outside the tile, a plain-HTML page.
guidance.When not to use:
- Filled, duotone or emoji icons, or icons from other sets mixed in: the system uses one outline style.
- An icon as the only content of a control without a name: use `IconButton` (it requires `label`).
- Status meaning carried by an icon alone: pair it with text, or use `ToneTag`.
- Most components take an `icon` prop (`Button`, `Chip`, `Menu` items, `EmptyState`); pass the name there rather than nesting an `<Icon>`.
guidance.Anatomy: **Icon**: `` — a 36 × 36 white tile (`--surface`), radius 11, `--sh-xs` plus a 1 px inset `--border-soft` ring — holding the mark as a 24 × 24 `` (the mark is sky blue `#2996D3`). `size` changes the tile only; the image stays 24 px.
guidance.Variants and sizes:
Size tokens (pass the number to `size`):

| Token | px | Typical use |
|---|---|---|
| `--icon-xs` | 12 | Chips, sort arrows, filter inputs |
| `--icon-sm` | 14 | Small buttons, tree children, dismiss `x` |
| `--icon-md` | 16 | Default: buttons, fields, banners |
| `--icon-nav` | 19 | Sidebar navigation |
| `--icon-tile` | 20 | Module tiles (`ModuleIcon` default) |
| `--icon-lg` | 24 | Empty states |

**Line icon names** (`IconName`) — every key of `line` in `packages/react/src/assets/icons.json`, the single source
of icon paths (in plain HTML, copy the value into `<svg class="lf-i" viewBox="0 0 24 24">…</svg>`): `settings` `chevron` `arrow` `plus` `search` `calendar` `refresh` `external` `share` `up` `down` `eye` `folder` `file` `filter` `download` `user` `logout` `collapse` `chevron-right` `chevrons-left` `chevrons-right` `check` `x` `minus` `sort` `trash` `chevron-left` `lock` `sparkles` `star` `bell` `users` `clipboard` `home` `mail` `file-search` `edit` `more` `info` `alert` `upload` `server` `database` `globe` `key` `shield` `clock` `play` `pause` `link` `copy` `layers` `archive` `list` `sliders` `plug` `card` `history` `restore` `send` `terminal` `cpu` `tag` `cloud` `building` `user_plus` `save` `grid`

Note the underscore in `user_plus`. `more` is three horizontal dots (row actions).

**Module icon names** (`ModuleIconName`): `ai` `auditor` `trust` `detect` `protect` `identify` `mylepide` `dashboards` `settings`
guidance.States: None. Icons follow their container's colour, so hover, selected and disabled colours come from the parent (for example ink-3 at rest, ink on hover, white inside a selected item).
guidance.Accessibility:
- All three are decorative: `Icon` and `ModuleIcon` are `aria-hidden="true"`, and `BrandMark`'s image has `alt=""`. The accessible name must come from visible text or an `aria-label` on the control.
- Next to `BrandMark`, show the product name as text ("Lepide").
- Never use an icon as the only indicator of state; selected states also change fill and ARIA attributes.

| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Use names from the lists above | Paste other SVGs or icon fonts |
| Let icons inherit colour from their container | Hard-code icon colours |
| 1.6 stroke outlines everywhere | Filled or mixed icon styles |
| `IconButton` with `label` for icon-only actions | A bare `<Icon>` inside a `<button>` with no name |
| `ModuleIcon` only for the product modules | Module glyphs as generic UI icons |
