components.title: KPI card
components.summary: Stat card with a label, a large value that counts up once, an optional delta chip, a foot line and a full-bleed sparkline. Imported from '@lepide/ds-react/charts'.

exports.name: KpiCard
exports.description: KPI card (03 § 8 `.lf-stat`): label, value that counts up once, delta chip, foot, sparkline.

guidance.When to use:
- The headline numbers at the top of a dashboard or report: total events, failed logons, open alerts, risk score.
- A number whose change over a period matters: add `delta` (and `spark` for the trend).
- A number that leads to detail: `onClick` makes the whole card a button (open the filtered report).
guidance.When not to use:
- Several values that need comparing against each other: use a `Chart` or a `DataTable`.
- Status of one object (enabled, healthy): use a `ToneTag` or `Chip`.
- Long labels or explanations: the card holds a short label and one foot line.
guidance.Anatomy:
`KpiCard` renders `<div class="lf-card lf-card--lift lf-stat">`: white, radius 20, 1 px `--border-soft`, padding 20 20 0 (20 all round when there is no sparkline), a two-column grid.
1. Label `.lf-stat__label` (top-left): 600 13/18 `--ink-2`.
2. Delta chip `.lf-stat__row` (top-right, when `delta` is set): an `.lf-chip--{deltaTone}` pill 24 tall, padding 0 9, with an optional 11 px up or down arrow (`deltaDir`) before the text.
3. Value `.lf-stat__value`: 600 34/40, −0.04em (`--type-kpi`, `--type-kpi-ls`), ink, tabular figures, 14 px above.
4. Foot `.lf-stat__foot` (when `foot` is set): 500 12.5/18 `--ink-3` — the comparison period or context ("vs last 7 days").
5. Sparkline `.lf-stat__apx` (when `spark` is set): a full-bleed 56 px `Sparkline` along the bottom edge (it extends 20 px past both sides of the padding), 10 px below the foot. `sparkColor` sets its colour (default `#1c4599`).

Lay KPI cards out in a `.kpis` grid: 4 columns with a 16 px gap (2 columns under 1280 px, 1 under 620 px); its children rise in with a 40 ms stagger. For three cards use `.kpis kpis--3` (3 columns, same breakpoints).
guidance.Variants and sizes:
`deltaTone` (default `flat`) — choose by meaning, not by direction:
| Tone | Chip | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `good` | `--success-bg`, `--success-text` | The change is good (fewer failed logons, more coverage) |
| `warn` | `--warning-bg`, `--warning-text` | Worth watching |
| `bad` | `--danger-bg`, `--danger-text` | The change is bad (more alerts) |
| `flat` | `--surface-3`, `--ink-3` | No meaningful change, or neutral |
| `brand` | `--brand-50`, brand, `--brand-100` ring | Neutral highlight (a new or informational figure) |

`deltaDir`: `up` or `down` arrow, independent of tone (a `down` arrow can be `good`).
guidance.States:
| State | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| First render | A numeric value counts up from 0 to the target over 1.2 s (quartic ease-out), then shows with thousands separators ("12,480"). Counting runs again when the value changes |
| Non-numeric value | Strings that aren't only digits, commas, dots and spaces ("98%", "4 h 12 m", "—") show as given, with no count-up |
| Hover | The card lifts 2 px and gets `--sh-md` and a `--border` border |
| Clickable (`onClick`) | Pointer cursor, `role="button"`, focusable; Enter or Space calls `onClick` |
| Not clickable | Default cursor (it still lifts on hover) |
| Reduced motion | No count-up: the final value shows immediately |

The count-up keeps the value's own decimal places: `12.5` counts to "12.5", `"1,234.50"` to "1,234.50". Strings with a unit or symbol ("12.5%", "12.5 GB") don't animate and are shown unchanged.
guidance.Accessibility:
- The label and the value are separate paragraphs, read in order: "Failed logons, 1,204".
- With `onClick` the card is a `role="button"` with `tabIndex=0` and keyboard activation; its accessible name is all its text, so keep the label short and meaningful.
- The delta arrow is `aria-hidden`; put the direction in the `delta` text when it matters ("+12%", "−3 alerts").
- Tone is never the only signal: the delta text says what changed.
- The sparkline has no text alternative; don't put information only there.
guidance.Do and don't:
| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Short label, sentence case: "Failed logons" | "TOTAL NUMBER OF FAILED LOGON EVENTS" |
| Tone by meaning: fewer failures is `good` even with a `down` arrow | Red for every decrease, green for every increase |
| Raw numbers as `value` (`1204`) so they count up and get separators | Pre-formatted numeric strings with units when a plain number works |
| Four cards in a `.kpis` row | Mixed-height cards (some with sparklines, some without) in one row |
| `foot` for the comparison period | Repeat the label in the foot |
guidance.Example:
```tsx import { KpiCard } from '@lepide/ds-react/charts';
openReport('failed-logons')} />
``` Plain HTML (with `@lepide/ds-css`, no count-up or sparkline): ```html

Failed logons

1,204

−18%

vs previous 7 days

```

components.title: Loading
components.summary: Loading feedback — shimmering skeleton table rows, a centred page spinner, and a determinate or indeterminate progress bar.

guidance.When to use:
- `SkeletonRows`: a table whose rows are loading. `DataTable` already renders it when `loading` is set; use it directly only in hand-built `.lf-table` markup.
- `PageLoader`: a whole page or a large panel is loading and there is no layout to sketch yet (route change, first load).
- `ProgressBar`: a long task with known progress (upload, export, scan) — or `indeterminate` when the task is running but progress is unknown.
guidance.When not to use:
- A button that is waiting on its own action: use `Button loading`.
- Short waits under about 300 ms: show nothing.
- Loading content that has a known shape other than a table (cards, KPI tiles): use the `.lf-loading` / `.lf-sk` skeleton classes on the real markup.
- A result: once the load finishes, replace the loader with the content, an `EmptyState` or an error.
guidance.Anatomy:
**SkeletonRows** (`<tbody class="sk-rows">`)
1. `rows` rows (default 7) × `cols` cells (default 5). Cells are 56 px tall with 0 16 padding (20 px on the first cell) and a 1 px `--border-soft` bottom border — the same height as real rows.
2. Each cell holds a 10 px pill bar (`.b`) whose width varies between 40 % and 89 % by position, with a `shimmer` gradient sweep (`--surface-3` → `#f9fafb` → `--surface-3`, 1.1 s, infinite).

**PageLoader** (`.page-loader`)
1. Full-height grid, content centred, 12 px gap.
2. Spinner (`.spinner-lg`): 32 px ring, 2.5 px `--surface-3` border with a `--brand` top segment, spins every 0.8 s.
3. Optional caption (`text`): 500 13/18 `--ink-3`.

**ProgressBar** (`.progress`)
1. Flex row, 10 px gap, min-width 120.
2. Track (`.progress__track`): 8 px pill, `--surface-3`, fills the row.
3. Fill (`.progress__fill`): `--brand`, width = `value` % (clamped to 0–100), animates width over 0.8 s.
4. Value (`.progress__val`): rounded percentage, 600 12/16 `--ink-2`, tabular numbers, min-width 34, right-aligned. Hidden when `indeterminate`.
guidance.Variants and sizes:
| Variant | Change |
|---|---|
| `ProgressBar indeterminate` | Fill fixed at 30 % width, sweeps from left to right every 1.1 s; no value text; no `aria-valuenow` |

`SkeletonRows` takes `rows` and `cols`; match `cols` to the table's column count.
guidance.States: None beyond the variants. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the shimmer, spin and sweep animations run once for 1 ms and stop, so the indicators stay visible but still.
guidance.Accessibility:
- `SkeletonRows` is `aria-hidden="true"`. Announce loading elsewhere — for example a "Loading…" caption or count (DataTable shows "Loading…" in its title counter) — and set `aria-busy="true"` on the table region if needed.
- `PageLoader` has `role="status"`, so the `text` caption is announced. Always pass `text` ("Loading reports…"); without it the status region is empty.
- `ProgressBar` has `role="progressbar"`, `aria-valuemin="0"`, `aria-valuemax="100"` and `aria-valuenow` (omitted when indeterminate). Pass `label` — it becomes `aria-label` ("Uploading licence file").
guidance.Do and don't:
| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Skeleton rows in the real table, same column count | A spinner in the middle of an empty table |
| `PageLoader` with a short caption | A bare spinner with no text |
| `ProgressBar` with `label` and real progress values | A fake progress bar that jumps to 99 % |
| `indeterminate` when progress is unknown | A determinate bar stuck at 0 % |
guidance.Example:
```tsx import { SkeletonRows, PageLoader, ProgressBar } from '@lepide/ds-react'; if (!report) return ; … {loading ? : {rows}}
``` Plain HTML (with `@lepide/ds-css`): ```html
42%
```

components.title: Menu
components.summary: A trigger plus an anchored popover menu of actions (.pop), with icons, separators, selected and danger items, and disabled items that explain why.

exports.name: Menu
exports.description:
A trigger plus an anchored `.pop` menu (03 § 14.2). `trigger` receives the toggle props.
align: 'right' (default, opens right-aligned under the trigger) | 'left' | 'up'.

guidance.When to use:
- A "more actions" button on a row, card or page header (`IconButton icon="more"`).
- A button that opens a short list of related actions ("Export ▾" → CSV, PDF, Schedule…).
- A small custom popover (a few checkboxes, a short form) anchored to a button: pass `children` instead of `items`.
guidance.When not to use:
- Choosing a value for a form field: use `Dropdown`, `SearchSelect` or `MultiSelect`.
- Switching views: use `Segmented`.
- A single action: use a `Button`.
- Navigation menus of the app shell (sidebar, account menu): those have their own components.
guidance.Anatomy:
1. Wrapper: `<span class="rel">`, inline-flex, `position: relative` — the anchor for the popover.
2. Trigger: whatever `trigger(props)` returns. Spread the props onto a button: `onClick` toggles the menu, plus `aria-expanded` and `aria-haspopup="menu"`.
3. Popover (`.pop`, `role="menu"`): absolute, 8 px below the trigger, right-aligned; `--surface` fill, 1 px `--border`, radius 14 (`--r-md`), padding 6, 2 px gap, `--sh-md`, z-index 40, min-width 200 (`width` raises the min-width). Opens with `pop-in` (fade and 4 px rise, `--t-fast`).
4. Item (`.pop__item`, `role="menuitem"`): full-width `<button>`, min-height 36 (`--menu-item-h`), padding 0 10, radius 8 (`--r-xs`), 10 px gap, 500 13/18 `--ink-2`; optional 15 px `--ink-3` icon, then the label.
5. Separator (`separator: true`): `.pop__sep`, 1 px `--border-soft` line with 4 6 margin.
6. Custom content (`children(close)`): replaces the item list; call `close()` when done. `.pop__head` (600 12/16 `--ink-3`, padding 6 10 4) is available for a small section heading.
guidance.Variants and sizes:
| `align` | Placement |
|---|---|
| `right` (default) | Below the trigger, right edges aligned; grows to the left |
| `left` | Below the trigger, left edges aligned (`.pop--left`) |
| `up` | Above the trigger, 6 px gap, right-aligned (`.pop--up`) — for triggers near the bottom of the viewport |

Item variants: `danger` (`.pop__item--danger`) for destructive actions; `selected` for the current choice in a menu of options.
guidance.States:
| State | Change |
|---|---|
| Item hover | `--surface-2` fill, `--ink` text |
| Item selected (`selected`) | `role="menuitemradio"` with `aria-checked="true"`: 600 `--ink` on `--surface-2`, with a 6 px `--brand` dot at the right |
| Danger item | `--danger-text`; hover `--danger-bg` |
| Disabled item | Native `disabled`: `--ink-4` text, no hover fill, `not-allowed` cursor; `reason` becomes its `data-tip` tooltip |
| Focus | 2 px brand focus outline on the focused item |
guidance.Accessibility:
- Opening the menu moves focus to the first enabled item (or the first `input` in custom content).
- Keyboard inside the menu: `ArrowDown` / `ArrowUp` move between enabled items and wrap; `Enter` / `Space` activate the focused item (the menu closes, then `onSelect` runs); `Home` / `End` jump to the first / last item; `Escape` closes. Type-ahead is not supported.
- Choosing an item, pressing Escape or calling `close()` from custom content returns focus to the trigger (the element with `aria-haspopup="menu"` — spread the trigger props onto it). Clicking outside closes the menu without moving focus.
- The trigger gets `aria-expanded` and `aria-haspopup="menu"` from the render props; always spread them. Give icon-only triggers a name (`IconButton label`).
- Pass `label` to name the menu (`aria-label` on `role="menu"`).
- Disabled items are skipped by arrow keys; their `reason` is shown by `TooltipHost` (mount it once) — say why the action is unavailable ("You need the Auditor role").
- Items with `selected` defined (true or false) render as `role="menuitemradio"` with `aria-checked`; the others are `role="menuitem"`. Use `Dropdown` when the choice is a form value.
guidance.Do and don't:
| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Verb labels in sentence case: "Export as CSV" | Nouns or Title Case |
| Put the destructive item last, after a separator, with `danger` | Mix delete between ordinary actions |
| Keep disabled items visible with a `reason` | Hide actions without explanation, or disable them silently |
| Seven items or fewer | Long scrolling menus — use a `Dropdown` with search |
| `align="up"` near the bottom of the screen | Menus that open off-screen |
guidance.Example:
```tsx import { Menu, IconButton, Button } from '@lepide/ds-react'; } items={[ { label: 'Edit report', icon: 'edit', onSelect: edit }, { label: 'Duplicate', icon: 'copy', onSelect: duplicate }, { label: 'Schedule', icon: 'clock', onSelect: schedule, disabled: !canSchedule, reason: 'Scheduling needs an SMTP server' }, { separator: true, label: '' }, { label: 'Delete report', icon: 'trash', danger: true, onSelect: confirmDelete }, ]} /> } items={[{ label: 'CSV', onSelect: () => exportAs('csv') }, { label: 'PDF', onSelect: () => exportAs('pdf') }]} /> ``` Plain HTML (with `@lepide/ds-css`): ```html
```

components.title: Modal
components.summary: Centred dialog with icon-tile head, scrolling form body and a footer of buttons; ConfirmDialog for yes/no questions; Steps for multi-step progress.

props.name: onSubmit
props.description: Makes body + footer a <form>: Enter in a field and a footer <Button type="submit"> call it (default submit is prevented).

exports.name: ConfirmDialog
exports.description: Confirm dialog (03 § 11.2): consequence as subtitle, Cancel + verb button.

guidance.When to use:
- `Modal` for a short, focused task that must finish or be cancelled before the user goes back to the page: create or edit one object, pick options, a 2–4 step setup.
- `ConfirmDialog` to confirm a destructive or irreversible action ("Delete 3 reports?") or any yes/no question that needs a deliberate answer.
- `Steps` inside a `Modal` (via the `steps` and `step` props) for a short multi-step dialog, or on its own above page content. `WizardCard` already renders it for full-page wizards.
guidance.When not to use:
- Reading or editing a record while keeping the list in view: use `Drawer` or `DetailPanel`.
- Long multi-step flows (more than about 4 steps, or steps with large forms): use a full-page `WizardCard`.
- Success or progress messages: use `useToast`. Never open a modal just to say "Saved".
- Nesting a second modal on top of a modal. A `ConfirmDialog` over a modal works (only the top-most overlay reacts to keys), but use it sparingly.
guidance.Anatomy:
1. Scrim: fixed, full window, `rgba(18,20,23,.28)` with a 3 px backdrop blur, z-index 80 (`--z-modal`), fades in.
2. Card `.modal__card`: white, radius 26 (`--modal-radius`), `--sh-lg`, max height `100dvh − 32px`, enters with `rise-in` (10 px rise, 250 ms).
3. Head `.mhead`, padding 24 24 16:
   - Icon tile `.mhead__ic`: 44 × 44, radius 14, `--brand-50` fill, brand icon (18 px), `--brand-100` inset ring. `tone="danger"` makes it `--danger-bg` with a red icon. Default icon `plus`; `icon={null}` removes the tile.
   - Title `<h3>`: 700 19/26, −0.025em, ink (`--type-modal-title`). Optional subtitle `<small>`: 500 13.5/20 `--ink-3`.
   - Close: a 34 px `.lf-btn--icon` with the `x` icon and `aria-label="Close"`, always shown.
4. Optional `Steps` row (when `steps` is passed), margin 0 24 20.
5. Body `.modal__form` (only when `children` is not null): flex column, gap 16, padding 0 24 24, scrolls. Fields rendered with `Field`/`TextField` (`.fld`) here get 46 px inputs on `--surface-2`, radius 14, and turn white with the brand `--ring` on focus.
6. Footer `.mfoot` (only when `footer` is passed): padding 16 24, top hairline `--border-soft`, `--surface-2` fill. Left: `footerHint` (600 12.5/16 `--ink-3`); right: `.mfoot__btns`, 8 px gap, buttons 40 tall.

`Steps`: an `<ol class="steps">`. Each step is a 24 px circle `.steps__n` (`--surface-3`, 700 11.5 `--ink-3`) and a 600 13/16 label in `--ink-4`. The current step uses the selected finish (`--sel-fill` + `--sel-ring`, white number) and ink label; done steps also use the selected finish and show a 12 px check. Steps are joined by 2 px lines, brand when reached, `--border` otherwise.
guidance.Variants and sizes:
| `size` | Width | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `lg` | 960 (`--modal-w-lg`) | Side-by-side layouts, pickers with a preview |
| `md` (default) | 760 (`--modal-w`) | Most create/edit forms |
| `sm` | 580 (`--modal-w-sm`) | Short forms (2–4 fields) |
| `xs` | 460 (`--modal-w-xs`) | Confirmations; `ConfirmDialog` always uses it |

All widths are `min(width, 100%)` inside a 16 px window padding.

`tone="danger"`: red icon tile. `ConfirmDialog` `destructive` (default `true`): `trash` icon on a red tile and a `danger-solid` confirm button; `destructive={false}`: `info` icon on a brand tile and a `primary` confirm button.

`Steps` `page`: adds `.steps--page` (no margin, wraps onto lines) for use above page content.
guidance.States:
| State | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Closed | `open={false}` renders nothing (no exit animation) |
| Opening | Portal into `document.body`; after 40 ms focus moves to the first `[data-autofocus]` element, else the first input/select/textarea in the body, else the first focusable element |
| Escape / scrim press | Calls `onClose` when `escapeCloses` (default `true`). `escapeCloses={false}` disables both; only the × (and your buttons) close it |
| Closing | Focus returns to the element that was focused when it opened |
| Busy confirm | `ConfirmDialog busy` shows a spinner in the confirm button and disables it |
| Step done | With `onStep`, done steps become clickable (`role="button"`, `tabIndex=0`, Enter or Space) and show a pointer; current and future steps are not clickable |

`ConfirmDialog` does not close itself: `onConfirm` must run the action and then call `onClose` (set `busy` while it runs).
guidance.Accessibility:
- The card is `role="dialog"` with `aria-modal="true"`. It is named by its title heading (`aria-labelledby`), so a string or a node `title` both work.
- Focus is trapped: Tab and Shift+Tab wrap between the first and last visible focusable elements. Escape only reaches the top-most overlay (`[data-overlay]`), so a dialog over a drawer closes on its own.
- Forms: pass `onSubmit` and give the primary footer button `type="submit"`. Body and footer become one `<form>` (`.modal__submit`, `display: contents`), so Enter in a field submits; validate inside `onSubmit`.
- `ConfirmDialog` starts focus on Cancel when `destructive` (the default), so Enter can't confirm by accident; with `destructive={false}` focus starts on the confirm button. Word `confirmLabel` as the exact action ("Delete 3 reports").
- `Steps` is an ordered list with `aria-label="Progress"`; the current step has `aria-current="step"`. Step labels are used as React keys, so they must be unique.
- Never put the only explanation of a consequence in the icon colour: the `message` says what happens.
guidance.Do and don't:
| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Title as a verb phrase: "Create report", "Delete schedule?" | "Dialog", "Warning", Title Case |
| Primary action last in `footer`, after Cancel | Primary first, or two primaries |
| Put the consequence in `ConfirmDialog` `message` ("This can't be undone.") | A bare "Are you sure?" with no consequence |
| `size="sm"` or `xs` for short content | A 760 px dialog around two fields |
| `escapeCloses={false}` only while unsaved input would be lost | Disabling Escape on every dialog |
| Close the dialog from `onConfirm` once the action succeeds | Leave a confirm dialog open after it worked |

- `crumbs` when the page sits below another page ("Reports › File server › Permission changes").

guidance.Accessibility:

- Breadcrumbs are a `nav` landmark named "Breadcrumb"; the current page is marked `aria-current="page"`; separators are `aria-hidden`.

components.title: Providers
components.summary: App-root setup. LepideProvider plugs in your router's link; ThemeProvider stores the light, dark or hc theme and applies it as <html data-theme>. Mount ToastProvider and TooltipHost once beside them.

exports.name: LepideProvider
exports.description: Optional. Pass your router's link, e.g. `link={({ to, ...p }) => <RouterLink to={to} {...p} />}`.

guidance.When to use:
Once, at the root of every app built with the Lepide Design System:

- `ThemeProvider`: always. It reads the saved theme, sets `data-theme` on `<html>` and gives you `useTheme()` for a theme switcher.
- `LepideProvider`: when the app has a client-side router, so kit links (breadcrumbs in `PageHeader`) navigate without a full page load. Optional: without it, links are plain `<a href>`.
- `ToastProvider` (from the toast docs): always, so `useToast()` works anywhere below it.
- `TooltipHost` (from the tooltip docs): always, once, so `data-tip` attributes, `IconButton` labels and disabled `Menu` item reasons show as tooltips.
guidance.When not to use:
- Do not nest a second `ThemeProvider` to theme part of a page: the theme is global (it is set on `<html>`). Sections cannot have their own theme.
- Do not mount `TooltipHost` or `ToastProvider` more than once.
- Do not set `data-theme` on `<html>` yourself after start-up; call `setTheme` so the stored value and the context stay in sync.
guidance.Anatomy:
**ThemeProvider**
1. On first render it reads `localStorage[storageKey]` (default key `"lepide.theme"`). `"dark"` and `"hc"` are kept; anything else, a missing value, or a storage error gives `"light"`.
2. After render, and on every change, it sets `document.documentElement.dataset.theme` (`<html data-theme="light|dark|hc">`). The token file switches every colour token on `:root[data-theme="dark"]` and `:root[data-theme="hc"]`.
3. `useTheme()` returns `{ theme, setTheme }`. `setTheme(t)` updates the context and writes `t` to `localStorage` (storage errors are ignored).

Themes: `light`, `dark` and `hc` (high contrast) are all stable; every text and icon colour pair meets WCAG AA in each (`npm run contrast`). High contrast uses a 3 px black focus outline and adds a 1 px border to cards.

**LepideProvider**
1. Holds the link component used by kit internals (today: `PageHeader` breadcrumbs, via `useLepideLink()`).
2. `link` receives `{ to, className, children }` and must render a link. Default: `<a href={to} className={className}>`.

**ToastProvider and TooltipHost** — not covered by this page's props; see the toast and tooltip docs. Put `TooltipHost` anywhere inside the tree (it renders the single floating tooltip), and wrap the app in `ToastProvider` (it renders the toast stack).

### Avoiding a theme flash
`ThemeProvider` applies the theme in an effect, after React has painted, so a dark-theme user would briefly see the light theme. Set the attribute before the CSS loads with an inline script in `<head>` that reads the same key:

```html
<head>
  <script>
    try {
      var t = localStorage.getItem('lepide.theme');
      document.documentElement.dataset.theme = t === 'dark' || t === 'hc' ? t : 'light';
    } catch (e) { document.documentElement.dataset.theme = 'light'; }
  </script>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/lepide.css"> <!-- @lepide/ds-css dist/lepide.css -->
</head>
```

If you pass a custom `storageKey`, use the same key in this script.
guidance.Variants and sizes: None.
guidance.States:
| Theme | `data-theme` | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Light | `light` | Stable (default) |
| Dark | `dark` | Stable |
| High contrast | `hc` | Stable |
guidance.Accessibility:
- Offer the theme choice in the UI (for example a Light / Dark / High contrast dropdown in the account menu). `ThemeProvider` does not follow the OS colour-scheme setting; the default is light.
- High contrast strengthens focus to a 3 px black outline; test keyboard focus in it.
- `TooltipHost` is what gives icon-only buttons their visible label; without it they still have an `aria-label` but sighted users get no tooltip.
- `LepideProvider` links must render a real `<a href>` (most router links do) so they work with the keyboard, middle-click and screen readers.
guidance.Do and don't:
| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Mount `ThemeProvider`, `LepideProvider`, `ToastProvider` and `TooltipHost` once at the root | Mount providers per page or per component |
| Add the inline `<head>` script so the saved theme applies before first paint | Accept a light flash on every load in dark mode |
| Switch themes with `useTheme().setTheme` | Write `data-theme` or `localStorage` directly |
| Offer all three themes in the theme picker | Hard-code colours that skip the theme tokens (they will fail in dark or high contrast) |

components.title: Radio group
components.summary: A set of 36 px radio option rows for choosing exactly one value; stacked by default or wrapped in a row.

exports.name: RadioGroup
exports.description: Radio group as Lepide Design System option rows (03 § 5.3).

guidance.When to use:
- Exactly one choice from two to about six options that should all be visible at once (report format, scope "This OU / Whole domain").
- When the options need a moment of comparison before choosing.
guidance.When not to use:
- More than about six options, or long lists: use `SelectField` / `SearchSelect`.
- A compact switch between views in a toolbar: use `Segmented`.
- Independent on/off choices: use `Checkbox` or `Toggle`.
guidance.Anatomy:
1. Group `.lf-radio` (`role="radiogroup"`): vertical flex, 2 px gap. `.lf-radio--row`: horizontal, wraps, 6 px row gap, 16 px column gap.
2. Option row `<label>`: min-height 36, padding 0 10, radius 8 (`--r-xs`), 10 px gap, 500 13/18 `--ink-2`.
3. Native radio input, 15 × 15, `accent-color: var(--brand)`.
4. Option label text.

Options accept strings or `{ value, label, disabled }`. Every input shares one `name` (generated with `useId()` unless you pass `name`).
guidance.Variants and sizes: None. Layout: stacked (default) or `row`. One size, 36 px rows.
guidance.States:
| State | Change |
|---|---|
| Hover | Row `--surface-2` |
| Checked | Row `--brand-50`, text `--ink`, brand-filled radio |
| Focus | Native radio focus ring (global 2 px brand outline) |
| Disabled option | Text `--ink-4`, no hover fill, not-allowed cursor |
guidance.Accessibility:
- Native radios: Tab moves into the group (to the checked option), ↑/↓/←/→ move and select within it, as the browser provides.
- Pass `ariaLabel` to name the group, or wrap it in `Field` with a label; the group has `role="radiogroup"`.
- The checked option is shown by the filled radio, not only the row tint.
guidance.Do and don't:
| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Preselect the safest or most common option | Leave a required group with no default unless a choice must be deliberate |
| Short, parallel labels: "CSV", "PDF", "Excel" | Long sentences as option labels |
| `row` for two or three short options | `row` with long labels that wrap unpredictably |
| `SelectField` past about six options | Ten radio rows in a dialog |
guidance.Example:
```tsx import { Field, RadioGroup } from '@lepide/ds-react'; ``` Plain HTML (with `@lepide/ds-css`): ```html
```

components.title: Search select
components.summary: Labelled select fields for long lists — SearchSelect picks one value with a search box past 8 options; MultiSelect picks several with checkboxes and an optional Select All.

exports.name: SearchSelect
exports.description: Searchable single select (03 § 4): a labelled <Dropdown> whose search box appears past `searchFrom` options.

exports.name: MultiSelect
exports.description: Multi-select with checkboxes and optional "Select All" (03 § 4).

guidance.When to use:
- `SearchSelect` for one value from a long list (users, servers, OUs, time zones) inside a form. It is a labelled `Dropdown` whose search box appears once there are more than `searchFrom` (default 8) options.
- `MultiSelect` for several values from a list (event types, recipients, servers to include). Add `selectAll` when picking everything is common.
guidance.When not to use:
- Short lists without a search need: use `SelectField` (same trigger, also auto-adds search past 8 options) — `SearchSelect` differs mainly in its default `placeholder="Select"` and the `pill` option.
- Two to five independent on/off choices that should all be visible: use a group of `Checkbox`es.
- Free-text entry or tags that are not in a list: `MultiSelect` cannot create new values.
guidance.Anatomy:
Both render inside `Field` (label, note, help, error) and use the `Dropdown` trigger and panel (see dropdown):

1. Trigger `.dd__trigger`: 46 px (`--field-h`), radius 14, `--surface-2`, chevron well at the right.
2. Panel `.dd__pop` in a portal: radius 14, padding 6, max height 320, flips above when needed.
3. Search `.dd__search` (38 px, placeholder "Search") — `SearchSelect`: past `searchFrom` options; `MultiSelect`: past 8 options (fixed).

`MultiSelect` specifics:
- Trigger text: the placeholder when empty; the labels joined with ", " for one or two values; "N selected" for three or more.
- Panel `.dd__pop--multi`; each row is a `.lf-check` checkbox (16 px box, `--check-size`) with min-height 38 (`--option-h`), padding 0 10, radius 10.
- Optional first row "Select All" (hidden while a search query is typed): checked when every option is selected, indeterminate when some are; it selects all non-disabled options or clears all.
- The panel stays open while you tick rows; it closes on an outside click or Esc.
guidance.Variants and sizes: None. One size, 46 px trigger. `SearchSelect` accepts `pill` for a 40 px white pill trigger (`.dd--pill`) in toolbars.
guidance.States:
| State | Change |
|---|---|
| Hover / open | Trigger turns white with `--border-2`; open adds `--brand-300` border and `--ring`, chevron rotates |
| Selected row | `SearchSelect`: `--brand-50`, `--brand-ink`, 600, check icon. `MultiSelect`: brand-filled checkbox, row `--brand-50` with `--brand-ink` text |
| Row hover | `--surface-2` |
| No search matches | "No matches for “…”" in `--ink-3` |
| Invalid (`error`) | Danger border and halo on the trigger, `.fld__err` message below |
| Disabled | Trigger `--ink-4`, opacity .75, does not open. Disabled options: `--ink-4`, not pickable (MultiSelect: disabled checkbox) |
guidance.Accessibility:
- `SearchSelect` inherits the full `Dropdown` keyboard model: ↓/↑/Enter/Space open; arrows, Home/End, PageUp/PageDown move; Enter picks; Esc closes; letters jump.
- `MultiSelect`: the trigger is a `button` with `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-expanded`; ↓ opens it. The panel is a `group` of native checkboxes: opening focuses the search box (past 8 options) or the first checkbox, ↑/↓ and Home/End move between them, Space toggles. Esc closes and returns focus to the trigger; a click outside closes without moving focus.
- The visible label is linked to the trigger with `htmlFor`; pass `ariaLabel` when there is no label.
- Selected rows always carry a check (icon or ticked box), never colour alone.
guidance.Do and don't:
| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| `selectAll` on long lists where "everything" is a common choice | Add your own "All" value to `options` |
| Keep option labels short and unique; the trigger shows at most two | Long labels that make "a, b" unreadable |
| Show the count of selected items elsewhere if the user needs the full list | Rely on the trigger to list every selection |
| `SearchSelect` for 9+ options a user will search by name | A plain list of 200 servers with no search |
guidance.Example:
```tsx
import { SearchSelect, MultiSelect } from '@lepide/ds-react';

<SearchSelect label="Server" value={server} onChange={setServer} options={servers} error={serverError} />

<MultiSelect label="Notify" note="Optional" placeholder="Choose recipients" selectAll
  value={recipients} onChange={setRecipients}
  options={[{ value: 'it', label: 'IT admins' }, { value: 'sec', label: 'Security team' }, { value: 'hr', label: 'HR' }]} />
```

components.title: Section nav
components.summary: Left-hand section navigation for settings-style pages, with a built-in dropdown that replaces it under 860 px. The current section gets the selected finish.

exports.name: SectionNav
exports.description:
Left-hand section navigation for settings-style pages, plus its narrow-screen replacement (a Dropdown shown under
860 px). Place it as the first child of `<div className="settings">`, followed by `<section className="settings__body">`.
The current item gets the selected finish and aria-current="page".

guidance.When to use:
- A page with several sections the user moves between, where each section is its own view: Settings categories, an admin area, a record with many sub-pages.
- Between 4 and about 20 sections. Group long lists with `group`.
guidance.When not to use:
- Two to five views of the same data: use `Segmented`.
- Sections inside a dialog: use `VerticalTabs`.
- Product-level navigation: that is the console sidebar (DESIGN.md §4.1).
guidance.Anatomy:
Place it as the first child of `<div className="settings">` (a 260 px sticky column + content grid) and put the content in `<section className="settings__body">`.
1. `nav.lf-card.snav`: white card, padding 14, sticky, scrolls when taller than the window.
2. Optional title `.snav__title` (700 15/22) and group headings `.snav__group` (600 11.5, `--ink-3`).
3. Items `.snav__item`: 38 px min-height, radius 10, 600 13/18 `--ink-2`, 16 px icon in `--ink-3`, optional badge `.snav__badge` (brand-50 pill).
4. Current item: `--sel-fill`, white text, `--sel-shadow`, `aria-current="page"`.
5. `.snav-select`: a pill `Dropdown` with the same options, shown instead of the card under 860 px.
guidance.Variants and sizes: Items are buttons (`onChange`) or router links (`to`, rendered through `LepideProvider`'s link, which receives `aria-current`). One size.
guidance.States:
| State | Change |
|---|---|
| Rest | `--ink-2` text, `--ink-3` icon |
| Hover | `--surface-2` background, `--ink` text |
| Current | Selected finish, white text and badge |
| Narrow (≤ 860 px) | The card hides; the dropdown shows |
guidance.Accessibility:
- The `nav` is named by `ariaLabel`, else `title`, else "Sections".
- The current item has `aria-current="page"` (never colour alone: the finish is a filled block).
- With `to`, items are real links, so they open in a new tab and announce as links.
guidance.Do and don't:
| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Keep labels to one or two words | Long sentences that wrap |
| Use `to` with your router so the URL changes per section | Hold the section only in component state when it should be linkable |
| Show counts with `badge` sparingly | A badge on every item |
guidance.Example:
```tsx import { SectionNav, PageHeader } from '@lepide/ds-react';
…cards…
``` Plain HTML (with `@lepide/ds-css`): ```html

Settings

General Mail server and delivery
…
```

components.title: Segmented
components.summary: Pill-shaped segmented control that switches between two to five sibling views (tabs mode) or data filters (pressed mode).

exports.name: Segmented
exports.description: mode "tabs" = role tablist (switches views); "pressed" = aria-pressed group (switches data).

guidance.When to use:
- Switching between two to five sibling views of the same page ("Overview · Activity · Permissions"): `mode="tabs"` (default).
- Switching the data a view shows without changing the view ("Last 7 days · 30 days · 90 days", "All · Failed"): `mode="pressed"`.
- Showing a count per option (`count`), for example the number of items in each status.
guidance.When not to use:
- More than five options, or option labels that are long: use `Dropdown`.
- Section navigation inside a settings dialog: use `VerticalTabs`.
- Navigating to a different page: use links or the sidebar.
- A single on/off setting: use `Toggle`.
- Triggering an action: use `Button`.
guidance.Anatomy:
1. Track: pill (`--r-pill`), `--surface-3` fill, 1 px `--border-soft` border, padding 4, gap 2 between segments.
2. Segment: a `<button>`, 32 px tall (`--seg-h`), padding 0 14, pill, 600 12.5/1 text in `--ink-3`, 7 px gap to the count. Segments share the width equally (`flex: 1`).
3. Optional count badge (`count`): `<b>` pill, 18 px tall, min-width 20, padding 0 6, 700 10.5/1, `rgba(18,20,23,.07)` fill, `--ink-3` text.
4. Selected segment: the selected finish — `--sel-fill` blue gradient, white text, `--sel-shadow`; its count badge turns white text on 18 % white.
guidance.Variants and sizes:
| Variant | Class | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| Default | `.seg` | Fills its container; segments share the width equally |
| `hug` | `.dash-switch` | Track and segments size to their labels (`flex: none`) |

| Mode | Container role | Segment state |
|---|---|---|
| `tabs` (default) | `role="tablist"` | `role="tab"`, `aria-selected`, roving `tabIndex` (only the selected segment is in the tab order) |
| `pressed` | `role="group"` | `aria-pressed`, every segment is in the tab order |

Any combination works: both layouts (`.seg` full width, `.dash-switch` with `hug`) style the selected segment from
`aria-selected="true"` (tabs) or `aria-pressed="true"` (filter), and both style count badges. A data filter with
counts — "All 6 · Open 4 · Resolved 2" above a table — is `mode="pressed"` (usually with `hug`), placed under the
page header (`PageHeader` children) or in the table card's toolbar.

One size: 32 px segments in a 42 px track.
guidance.States:
| State | Change |
|---|---|
| Rest | `--ink-3` text on the `--surface-3` track |
| Hover | Text turns `--ink` |
| Selected | `--sel-fill`, white text, `--sel-shadow` |
| Focus | 2 px brand outline (`--focus-outline`), offset 2 px |
| Disabled (`item.disabled`) | Native `disabled`; skipped by arrow-key navigation |

Background, colour and shadow transition over `--t-base` / `--t-fast`; reduced motion shortens them to 1 ms.
guidance.Accessibility:
- Pass `ariaLabel` to name the group ("Report period"); it becomes `aria-label` on the track.
- Keyboard (on the track): `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` move the selection to the previous / next enabled segment and wrap; `Home` / `End` select the first / last enabled segment. Selection follows focus: the arrow keys call `onChange` immediately and focus moves to the new selected segment.
- `mode="tabs"` exposes the tablist pattern but does not set `aria-controls`; give the panel `role="tabpanel"` and an `aria-labelledby` yourself if needed.
- Selection is not colour alone: the selected segment has a filled, raised finish and the ARIA state.
guidance.Do and don't:
| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Two to five short, sentence-case labels | Long labels that wrap or truncate |
| `mode="pressed"` when the control filters the data on screen | `role="tab"` semantics for a data filter |
| `hug` when the control sits beside other content | A full-width `.seg` squeezed into a toolbar |
| Always keep one segment selected | Use a segmented control as a multi-select |
| Name the group with `ariaLabel` | Rely on surrounding text to explain what it switches |

components.title: Setting row
components.summary: A settings list row with a title and help text on the left and a control (usually a Toggle) on the right, separated by hairlines.

exports.name: SettingRow
exports.description: A settings row: title + help text on the left, a control (often a Toggle) on the right.

guidance.When to use:
- Settings pages and settings cards: one row per setting, each with a title, an optional one-line explanation and its control.
- The control is usually a `Toggle`; a small `Dropdown` (`size="sm"`), `NumberField` or `Button` also fits.
guidance.When not to use:
- Data entry forms with many fields: use `Field` / `TextField` in a `.page-form`.
- Read-only key/value details: use a key/value list, not setting rows.
guidance.Anatomy:
1. Row `.setrow`: flex, items centred, space-between, 16 px gap, padding 14 0, 1 px `--border-soft` bottom border (none on the last row).
2. Text `.setrow__text`: title `<b>` 600 13.5/20 `--ink`; optional help `<span>` 400 12.5/18 `--ink-3`, on its own line.
3. Control slot: a `.row` wrapper (horizontal flex, items centred, 8 px gap) holding `children`, so several small controls line up.
guidance.Variants and sizes: None. One size.
guidance.States: None of its own; the control carries hover, focus and disabled states.
guidance.Accessibility:
- The title is plain text, not a `<label>`. Give the control its own accessible name that matches the title (e.g. `Toggle label="Email alerts"`).
- Keep the help text short; it is not linked to the control with `aria-describedby`.
guidance.Do and don't:
| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Title names the setting ("Email alerts"); help says what happens when it is on | Put the explanation in the title |
| One control per row | Several unrelated controls in one row |
| Group related rows in one card with a heading | One endless list of unrelated settings |
guidance.Example:
```tsx import { SettingRow, Toggle, Dropdown } from '@lepide/ds-react';
``` Plain HTML (with `@lepide/ds-css`): ```html
Email alertsSend an e-mail when a critical alert is raised.
```

components.title: Sign in
components.summary: The whole sign-in page — glass card with the form (email, password, keep me signed in) and an illustration panel with highlight slides. Validation, loading and error states are built in.

props.name: onSubmit
props.description:
Called with valid input. Return a promise to show the loading state; reject (or throw) an Error to show its
message under the password field. Resolving shows "Signed in".

props.name: forgotPasswordTo
props.description: Link for "Forgot password?" (rendered through LepideProvider's link). Omit to hide it.

props.name: requestAccessTo
props.description: Link for "Request access" in the footer. Omit to hide the footer.

props.name: slides
props.description: Highlights shown on the illustration panel, with dots to switch between them.

props.name: defaultKeepSignedIn
props.description: Initial state of "Keep me signed in".

guidance.When to use: - The product's sign-in page. It is a whole page: render it outside the console shell and outside any card.
guidance.When not to use:
- Re-authenticating inside the console (session expired, confirm with password): use a `Modal` with a `PasswordField`.
- Sign-up, password reset or one-time-code pages: build them from the same `.login-page` classes (see the static
  `examples/html/sign-in.html`); the component covers sign-in only.
guidance.Anatomy:
1. Page `.login-page` → `.stage` → `.auth`: a 1120 px glass card (`--glass-strong`, radius 32) in two halves.
2. Form half: `BrandMark` (52 px tile), eyebrow (`.auth-eyebrow`), title 600 30/38 (`h1`), optional subtitle.
3. Fields: 48 px tall, radius 14, a leading 18 px icon (`.lead-ico`); the password has a show/hide eye button.
   "Forgot password?" sits on the label row when `forgotPasswordTo` is set.
4. "Keep me signed in" checkbox, then a 50 px primary pill button with an arrow.
5. Footer "New to Lepide? Request access" when `requestAccessTo` is set.
6. Illustration half `.auth__art` (radius 24, radial blue gradient): the shield illustration (or `art`), and when
   `slides` are given, the current slide's kicker, title and text with dots to switch (2 or more slides).
guidance.Variants and sizes: One layout. Below 860 px the illustration panel hides and the form fills the card.
guidance.States:
| State | Change |
|---|---|
| Field error | Red border on the input and a message with an alert icon under it; the button shakes once; focus moves to the first invalid field |
| Loading | While `onSubmit`'s promise is pending: spinner, "Signing in…", `aria-busy`; further submits are ignored |
| Done | Promise resolved: check icon, "Signed in" |
| Failed | Promise rejected: the error's message under the password field ("Wrong email or password."), focus on the password |
guidance.Accessibility:
- Labels are real `<label for>`s; errors are linked with `aria-describedby` and announced (`role="alert"`).
- The eye button is `aria-pressed` and named "Show password" / "Hide password".
- `autocomplete="username"` and `"current-password"` let password managers fill the form.
- Slide copy is `aria-live="polite"`; each dot is named "Show highlight 2 of 3: Lepide Auditor".
guidance.Do and don't:
| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Reject with a short, plain message: "Wrong email or password." | Say which of the two was wrong |
| Keep two or three highlight slides with one-line text | Marketing paragraphs on the panel |
| Pass router paths to `forgotPasswordTo` / `requestAccessTo` (rendered through `LepideProvider`'s link) | Hard-code `<a>` tags that reload the app |

components.title: Text field
components.summary: Labelled form fields for dialogs and page forms — 46 px soft-filled controls with a label, optional note, help text and inline error.

exports.name: Field
exports.description:
Dialog / form field wrapper (03 § 3.2): label, optional note, control, inline error.
Use inside <Modal> (class modal__form) or any container with class "page-form".

exports.name: TextField
exports.description: Labelled text input in the dialog-field style.

exports.name: PasswordField
exports.description: Password with show/hide (accessible name "Show password" / "Hide password").

exports.name: NumberField
exports.description: Numeric field with step buttons (03 § 19).

guidance.When to use:
- `TextField` for any single-line value in a dialog or page form: names, e-mail addresses, paths, descriptions.
- `PasswordField` for secrets the user types; it adds a show/hide eye button.
- `NumberField` for bounded integers or counts (retention days, thresholds) where stepping by `step` is useful.
- `TextAreaField` for multi-line free text (notes, descriptions, e-mail bodies).
- `Field` on its own to give any other control (a `Dropdown`, `MultiSelect`, `Checkbox` group, custom widget) the same label, note, help and error layout.
guidance.When not to use:
- Toolbar filters and searches above tables or lists: use `PillInput` / `SearchField` (40 px pill).
- Choosing from a fixed list: use `SelectField`, `SearchSelect` or `RadioGroup`, never a text field with instructions.
- Outside a `.modal__form` or `.page-form` container: the 46 px field styling of the `input`, `textarea` and `select` inside `.fld` is scoped to those two containers, so the control falls back to browser/global styles elsewhere. `<Modal>` and `WizardCard` already provide the container.
guidance.Anatomy:
1. Wrapper `.fld`: vertical flex, 7 px gap, `min-width: 0`.
2. Label `.fld__lbl` (`<label htmlFor>`): 600 13/18 `--ink`. Optional `note` renders as an `<em>` after it: 500 12/16 `--ink-4`, 8 px gap, not italic — use it for "Optional", units or limits.
3. Control: height 46 (`--field-h`), padding 0 14 (`--field-px`), radius 14 (`--field-radius`), 1 px `--border`, fill `--surface-2`, text 500 14/20 `--ink`, placeholder 400 `--ink-4`. Textarea: min-height 84, padding 12 14 (resizes vertically in `.page-form`, not in `.modal__form`).
4. Help text `.help` (only when there is no error): 500 12/16 `--ink-3`.
5. Error `.fld__err`: 600 12/16 `--danger-text` with a 14 px circled "!" icon, fades up. Replaces the help text.

`PasswordField`: the input sits in `.fld-pw` with 48 px right padding; a 34 px round `.eye` button (17 px eye icon, `--ink-3`) is inset 6 px from the right edge.

`NumberField`: `.fld-num` row with 6 px gaps — the input (tabular numerals, `inputMode="numeric"`), then a 28 px round − button and a 28 px round + button (1 px `--border`, white, 14 px icons), then an optional `suffix` in `.muted.text-sm`.

Two fields side by side: wrap them in `<div className="fld-row">` (grid 1fr 1fr, 14 px gap; one column under 620 px).
guidance.Variants and sizes: None. One size: 46 px controls (`--field-h`); textarea min-height 84 px.
guidance.States:
| State | Change |
|---|---|
| Hover | Border `--border-2` (not when disabled) |
| Focus | Fill `--surface` (white), border `--brand-300`, `--ring` (3 px brand halo); no outline |
| Invalid (`error` set) | `.fld.is-bad`: danger border, white fill, `0 0 0 3px rgba(207,58,63,.12)` halo, one `shake`; `.fld__err` message below; control gets `aria-invalid="true"` |
| Disabled | Text `--ink-4`, opacity .8, `not-allowed` cursor (`.page-form`; in `.modal__form` the disabled rule covers `select` only) |
| Password visible | Eye button `aria-pressed="true"`, icon `--brand-ink`; hover `--surface-3` fill |
| Number at a bound | − is disabled when `value <= min`, + when `value >= max`; typed values are not clamped, step buttons are |
guidance.Accessibility:
- The label is a real `<label for>`; each field generates an id with `useId()` unless you pass `id`.
- The error renders with `role="alert"`, so it is announced when it appears, and the control gets `aria-invalid`.
- `Field` only links the label to a control when you pass `htmlFor` and give the control that `id`.
- The eye button is `type="button"` with `aria-label` "Show password" / "Hide password" and `aria-pressed`.
- Number step buttons are labelled "Decrease" / "Increase". Typing a non-number is ignored (the previous value is kept); clearing the input calls `onChange('')`.
- Help text is not wired to the control with `aria-describedby`; keep critical instructions in the label or note.
- Focus uses the 3 px `--ring` instead of the global outline; in high contrast the ring is the theme's.
guidance.Do and don't:
| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Put fields inside `<Modal>`'s form or a `.page-form` container | Render `TextField` in a bare `div` and expect the 46 px style |
| Short label in sentence case; "Optional" or units in `note` | Long instructions in the label or placeholder |
| Show one specific error under the field ("Enter a valid e-mail address") | Only colour the border red, or show errors in a toast |
| `.fld-row` for two short related fields (first and last name) | Three or more fields in one row |
| `NumberField` with `min`/`max` for bounded counts | A free text field for numbers |
guidance.Example:
```tsx import { Modal, TextField, PasswordField, NumberField, TextAreaField, Button } from '@lepide/ds-react';
``` Plain HTML (with `@lepide/ds-css`): ```html
Enter a fully qualified domain name.
days
```

components.title: Tile picker
components.summary: A grid of selectable tiles (icon or logo, title, one-line description) for choosing a type or source — single choice by default, or several with multiple.

exports.name: TilePicker
exports.description:
A grid of selectable tiles (≥200 px each) for choosing a type or source with a short description — e.g. "Windows
file server / NetApp / SharePoint Online". Single choice by default (radio semantics); `multiple` for several.

guidance.When to use:
- Picking one type from 2–9 options that each need a short explanation or a logo: data-source type, policy template, report kind — typically the first step of a wizard.
- `multiple` when several can be chosen (connectors to enable).
guidance.When not to use:
- Plain options without descriptions: use `RadioGroup` (one) or a checkbox list / `MultiSelect` (many).
- Switching views: use `Segmented`.
guidance.Anatomy:
1. `.pick-grid` (`role="radiogroup"`, or `group` with `multiple`): auto-fill grid of tiles at least 200 px wide, 10 px gap.
2. Tile `.pick` (a button): padding 14, radius 14, 1 px `--border`, white.
3. `.pick__ic`: 36 px `--brand-50` tile with an 18 px brand icon, or a 24 px logo (`image`).
4. `.pick__text`: title `b` 700 13.5/18 `--ink`, description 500 12/16 `--ink-3`.
5. Chosen: `--brand` border and an 18 px round `.pick__check` with the selected finish at the top right.
guidance.Variants and sizes: Single (radio) or `multiple` (pressed buttons). One size; the grid reflows.
guidance.States:
| State | Change |
|---|---|
| Hover | `--border-2`, `--sh-sm`, lifts 1 px |
| Chosen | Brand border + check (`aria-checked` or `aria-pressed`) |
| Disabled | Opacity .5, not-allowed cursor |
guidance.Accessibility:
- Single choice is a `radiogroup` of `role="radio"` buttons with `aria-checked`; multiple is a `group` of `aria-pressed` buttons.
- `ariaLabel` is required — it names the group ("Source type").
- The check mark adds a non-colour cue to the chosen tile.
guidance.Do and don't:
| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| A one-line description per tile | Paragraphs in tiles |
| Logos for third-party sources (`image`) | Mixing logos and icons in one grid |
| Pre-select the most common option when there is one | Leave a required single choice with nothing chosen and no hint |
guidance.Example:
```tsx import { TilePicker } from '@lepide/ds-react'; setSource(v as string)} options={[ { value: 'windows', label: 'Windows file server', description: 'NTFS shares on Windows Server', icon: 'server' }, { value: 'netapp', label: 'NetApp filer', description: 'CIFS shares on ONTAP', icon: 'database' }, { value: 'spo', label: 'SharePoint Online', description: 'Sites and document libraries', icon: 'cloud' }, ]} /> ``` Plain HTML (with `@lepide/ds-css`): ```html
```

components.title: Toast
components.summary: Notifications from one call, toast({...}). They show as a card stack in the bottom-right corner, or as a nudge callout beside the control the user just clicked when an error or warning answers that click.

exports.name: useToast
exports.description: Returns toast(input): shows a card or nudge and returns a handle to update or dismiss it.

guidance.When to use:
- Confirm that something finished: "Report saved", "3 users disabled".
- Report a background result the user should know about but needn't act on immediately.
- Show progress of a short async action with `loading: true`, then `update()` it with the result.
- Tell the user why the button they just pressed didn't work ("Add at least one column"): an `error` or `warning` raised right after a click automatically appears as a nudge beside that button.
- Offer one or two follow-ups ("Undo", "Open report") with `actions`.
guidance.When not to use:
- Field validation: show the error on the field (`Field` `error`), not in a toast.
- Information the user must read or decide on before continuing: use `ConfirmDialog` or a `Banner`.
- Persistent page state (a licence expires, a connector is down): use a `Banner`.
- Long text: a toast holds a title and one or two lines.
guidance.Anatomy:
Set-up: wrap the app once in `<ToastProvider>`; call `const toast = useToast()` in any component below it. Outside a provider `toast()` does nothing.

**Card stack** (`.ntf-stack`, rendered into `document.body`): fixed 20 px from the right and bottom edges (right 16, bottom 92 under 860 px), width `min(360px, 100vw − 32px)` (`--toast-w`), z-index 100 (`--z-toast`). Each card `.ntf`:
1. White, 1 px `--border`, radius 14 (`--r-md`), shadow `0 1px 2px rgba(18,20,23,.06), 0 16px 36px -14px rgba(18,20,23,.26)`; inner padding 12 42 14 12.
2. Tone tile `.ntf__tile`: 36 × 36, radius 11, tone background and tone ink, 17 px icon (`check` for success, `info` for info, `alert` for warning and error). While `loading`, a spinner replaces the icon. Error tiles pulse a red glow twice.
3. `.ntf__title`: 700 13.5/20 ink. It shows `title`, or `message` when there is no title. A repeated notification adds a count pill `.ntf__count` ("×3", 800 11 white on the tone dot colour).
4. `.ntf__msg`: 500 12.5/18 `--ink-2`, shown under the title only when both `title` and `message` are given.
5. `.ntf__acts`: up to two small (`sm`) buttons, 8 px gap, 10 px above; `primary: true` makes one the primary button.
6. Dismiss `.ntf__x`: 28 px round, 8 px from the top-right, `--ink-4` icon, `aria-label="Dismiss"`.
7. Timer bar `.ntf__bar`: 3 px along the bottom edge in the tone dot colour, shrinking left to right; the card closes when it ends. Not shown while `loading`.

**Nudge** (`.nudge`, one at a time): a 320 px callout (`min(320px, 100vw − 16px)`) placed 12 px above the control (below it when there is less than 8 px of room above), with a 12 px rotated-square arrow pointing at the control's centre. White, 1 px `--border`, radius 14, `--sh-lg`, z-index 140 (`--z-nudge`), padding 12 40 17 12. Contents: a 30 px tone tile (radius 10, 16 px icon), the `title` as an uppercase context line `.nudge__ctx` (700 11/16, +0.04em, tone ink), the `message` (700 13/19 ink), actions, a × and a 2 px timer bar inset 14 px from each side. The control itself gets `.is-nudged` for 1.4 s: a 0.45 s horizontal shake and a red ring pulse.
guidance.Variants and sizes:
| `variant` | Tile and bar | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `info` (default for cards) | `--brand-50` / `--brand-ink`, bar `--brand-400` | Neutral news, background jobs started |
| `success` | `--success-bg` / `--success-text`, bar `--success-dot` | Something finished |
| `warning` | `--warning-bg` / `--warning-text`, bar `--warning-dot` | Done with caveats, or a soft block |
| `error` | `--danger-bg` / `--danger-text`, bar `--danger-dot`; `role="alert"` | Failed actions |

A nudge with no `variant` uses the `error` tone.

Where it shows (`anchor`):
| `anchor` | Result |
|---|---|
| `'auto'` (default; `null` behaves the same) | `error` or `warning` raised within 1.2 s of a click on a `button`, `[role="button"]`, `a[href]` or `[role="menuitem"]` that is still visible → nudge beside it. Everything else → card |
| `'corner'` | Always a card |
| an `HTMLElement` or a CSS selector | Nudge beside that element if it is visible (any variant); otherwise a card |

Durations (provider `duration`, default 5000 ms):
| Form | Default | Override |
|---|---|---|
| Card, info / success / warning | `duration` (5 s) | `ToastInput.duration` |
| Card, error | `duration × 1.4` (7 s) | `ToastInput.duration` |
| Card, `loading: true` | No timer until `update()` sets `loading: false` | — |
| Nudge | `duration × 1.6` (8 s) | `ToastInput.duration` |
guidance.States:
| State | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Enter | Card slides up from below the corner and fades in; nudge scales in from its arrow (`nudge-in`, 0.4 s) |
| Stacked | Newest in front; each older card sits 12 px higher and 5 % smaller with its content hidden; 3 visible, at most 5 kept (a 6th pushes the oldest out) |
| Hover or focus on the stack | Cards fan out into a column with 10 px gaps; all timers pause |
| Hover on a nudge | Its timer pauses |
| Repeat | Same `title`, `message` and `variant` while the card is still showing → no new card; the count goes up, the tile pops and the timer restarts. A repeat on the same nudge anchor bumps the nudge |
| Drag | Drag a card right more than 90 px to dismiss it; less springs back |
| Leave | Card slides out to the right and fades, removed after 360 ms |
| Nudge close | ×, Escape, a mouse press anywhere outside it, any typing (`input` event), an action button, or the timer. Escape is stopped there, so a dialog behind the nudge stays open |
| Nudge anchor gone | If the control disappears within 400 ms (a menu closed, a step changed) the message moves to the card stack; later it just closes. The nudge follows the control while it scrolls or moves |
| Reduced motion | No slide, shake, pop or nudge animation; cards still appear and disappear |

`ToastHandle` (returned by every `toast()` call):
- `update(patch)` merges `patch` into the notification, restarts its timer and pops its tile. If the card was already dismissed, it shows again as a new card with the merged content.
- `dismiss()` closes it now.

`ToastAction`: `{ label, onClick?, primary? }`. A click closes the notification first, then runs `onClick`. Only the first two actions render. Action labels are React keys, so keep them unique.

`loading` is only drawn in the card stack; a nudge always shows its tone icon and timer.
guidance.Accessibility:
- The stack is `role="region"` with `aria-label="Notifications"`. Error cards are `role="alert"` (announced immediately); other cards are `role="status"`. A nudge is always `role="alert"`.
- The timer pauses while keyboard focus is inside the stack, so users can Tab to actions and the × without the card closing.
- Every × has `aria-label="Dismiss"`. Dragging is optional; the × does the same.
- Don't put the only route to something important in a toast: it disappears. Repeat critical results on the page.
guidance.Do and don't:
| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Short past-tense messages: "Report saved" | "Success!", "Operation completed successfully." |
| `title` + `message` when the message needs context | Long paragraphs or lists |
| `loading: true`, then `update({ loading: false, variant: 'success', message })` | A "working…" toast followed by a second "done" toast |
| Let an error after a click become a nudge (default `anchor`) | Force `anchor: 'corner'` for errors that explain a button press |
| One primary action at most ("Undo", "Open") | Two primary actions, or more than two actions |
| Field errors on the field | Toasts for each invalid field |

components.title: Toggle
components.summary: 38 × 22 on/off switch for settings that take effect immediately; always has an accessible label.

exports.name: Toggle
exports.description: Toggle switch (03 § 5.1).

guidance.When to use:
- A single setting that is on or off and applies as soon as it is flipped (enable alerts, auto-refresh, mask sensitive data).
- Rows in a settings list — put it in a `SettingRow`, which supplies the visible title and help text.
guidance.When not to use:
- A choice that is only applied after "Save" or "Apply" in a form: use `Checkbox`.
- Choosing between named options ("Daily / Weekly"): use `RadioGroup` or `Segmented`.
- Agreeing to terms or selecting rows: use `Checkbox`.
guidance.Anatomy:
1. Track: `<button class="lf-toggle">`, 38 × 22 (`--toggle-w` × `--toggle-h`), pill radius, no border. Off `--toggle-off`, on `--brand`.
2. Knob (`::after`): 16 px white (`--surface`) circle, 3 px inset, soft two-layer shadow. Slides 16 px to the right when on (250 ms `--ease-out`).

The component renders no visible text; the label is supplied for screen readers only. Place visible text next to it (or use `SettingRow`).
guidance.Variants and sizes: None. One size, 38 × 22.
guidance.States:
| State | Change |
|---|---|
| Off | Track `--toggle-off`; hover `--toggle-off-hover` (darker greys in the dark theme) |
| On | `aria-checked="true"`, track `--brand`, knob at the right |
| Pressed | Knob stretches to 20 px wide (toward the centre when on) |
| Focus | Global 2 px brand outline (`--focus-outline`), offset 2 px |
| Disabled | Opacity .45, not-allowed cursor (inline style), `disabled` attribute; clicks do nothing |
guidance.Accessibility:
- Renders `<button type="button" role="switch" aria-checked>`; Space and Enter toggle it (native button behaviour).
- `label` is required and becomes `aria-label`. When a visible title sits next to it, use the same words.
- `id` lets you point a visible `<label htmlFor>` or `aria-describedby` at it.
- On/off is shown by knob position as well as colour.
guidance.Do and don't:
| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Apply the change immediately and confirm with a toast if it has side effects | Require a Save button after flipping a toggle |
| `label` that names the setting: "Email alerts" | `label="Toggle"` or "On/Off" |
| Use inside `SettingRow` with a short help line | A toggle with no visible text anywhere |
| `Checkbox` inside forms that are submitted | Mix toggles and checkboxes for the same kind of choice in one form |
guidance.Example:
```tsx
import { Toggle, SettingRow } from '@lepide/ds-react';

<SettingRow title="Email alerts" help="Send an e-mail when a critical alert is raised.">
  <Toggle label="Email alerts" checked={alerts} onChange={setAlerts} />
</SettingRow>
```

Plain HTML (with `@lepide/ds-css`):
```html
<button type="button" class="lf-toggle" role="switch" aria-checked="true" aria-label="Email alerts"></button>
```

components.title: Tooltip
components.summary: One floating tooltip for the whole app. Mount TooltipHost once; any element with data-tip, and every icon-only button with an aria-label, shows its label on hover or keyboard focus.

guidance.When to use:
- Name an icon-only control: every `IconButton` (`.lf-btn--icon`) already gets its `label` as a tooltip, with no extra code.
- Give a short hint on any other element: add `data-tip="…"` (e.g. a truncated name, a status icon, a disabled reason on a wrapper).
guidance.When not to use:
- Information the user needs to complete a task: put it on the page (help text under a field, a `Banner`).
- Rich content, links or buttons: a tooltip is plain text, one line, and can't be hovered or clicked. Use a `Menu` or a popover.
- Touch-only interfaces: tooltips need hover or keyboard focus.
- Repeating a visible text label.
guidance.Anatomy:
Mount `<TooltipHost />` once, near the root (next to `ToastProvider`). It renders one `<div class="tipfloat" role="tooltip">` and listens on the document; no wrapper component is needed per element.

What shows a tooltip — the nearest ancestor of the hovered or focused element that matches:
1. `[data-tip]` — text is the `data-tip` value.
2. `.lf-btn--icon` (`IconButton`, the × in modals and drawers, icon buttons in DataTable row actions) or `.dock-toggle` — text is the `aria-label`.

`data-tip` wins over `aria-label` when both are present. Elements with neither show nothing.

Bubble `.tipfloat`: fixed, z-index 120 (`--z-tooltip`), ink fill (`--ink`), white 600 12/16 text, padding 6 10, radius 8 (`--r-xs`), one line (`white-space: nowrap`), `pointer-events: none`.

Placement: centred 8 px above the element; below it when there is less than 8 px of room above; kept 8 px inside the window edges. Inside the side dock (`.lf-dock`) it sits 10 px to the right of the element, vertically centred.
guidance.Variants and sizes: None.
guidance.States:
| State | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Hover | Appears after 350 ms over the same element; fades in with a 2 px rise over 150 ms (`--t-fast`) |
| Keyboard focus | Appears immediately when the element receives `:focus-visible` (not on mouse focus) |
| Hide | On mouse leaving to a non-tip element, focus out, any mouse press, Escape, any scroll (including inner scroll containers) and window resize |
guidance.Accessibility:
- The tooltip is decorative support: the accessible name comes from the element's own `aria-label` (an `IconButton` `label` is required for this reason). Don't rely on `data-tip` as the only name of an icon-only control — give it an `aria-label` too.
- It appears on keyboard focus as well as hover, and Escape hides it.
- The bubble has `role="tooltip"` but is not linked with `aria-describedby`; screen readers read the element's label, not the bubble.
- Keep the text short (a few words); it never wraps.
guidance.Do and don't:
| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Mount `<TooltipHost />` once per app | One `TooltipHost` per page or per component |
| `IconButton label="Refresh"` and let the tooltip follow | Add `data-tip` that repeats the same label |
| `data-tip` for short hints: "Read-only — managed by policy" | Sentences, instructions, or anything with a link |
| Sentence case, no trailing full stop | Title Case Tooltips. |
guidance.Example: ```tsx import { ToastProvider, TooltipHost, IconButton, Icon } from '@lepide/ds-react'; // Once, at the root: // Anywhere below: {/* tooltip: "Refresh" */} ``` Plain HTML (with `@lepide/ds-css`, `TooltipHost` mounted): ```html … ```

components.title: Tree
components.summary: Folder / report tree for a hub page — top-level folders with counts, expandable groups and nested items. The current row gets the selected finish.

exports.name: Tree
exports.description:
Folder / report tree. Top-level rows are 38 px with counts; the current row (value) gets the selected finish.
Rows with children expand and collapse. Keyboard: ↑/↓ move, → expands, ← collapses or goes to the parent, Home/End.

guidance.When to use:
- The left column of a hub (DESIGN.md §4.2 "Reports hub"): pick a folder, the table on the right shows its contents.
- Hierarchies two or three levels deep with counts.
guidance.When not to use:
- Flat lists of sections: use `SectionNav`.
- Choosing items for a form: use `MultiSelect` or a checkbox list.
guidance.Anatomy:
Put it in a card: `<Card title="Folders" className="folders">` (the reports layout `.reports` gives the 288 px column).
1. `ul.tree` (`role="tree"`), 2 px between rows.
2. Top-level rows: 38 px, radius 10, 600 13 `--ink-2`; a 16 px `folder` icon (or a chevron `.sign` when the row has children); label; count pill `.n` (20 tall, `--surface-3`, 700 11 tabular).
3. Nested rows: inside `ul[role="group"]`, indented 18 px behind a `--border` hairline; 32 px, radius 8, 500 13 `--ink-2`, 13–14 px icons in `--ink-4`. Nested rows with children are `li.grp`.
4. Current row (`value`): top level — selected finish, white text and count; nested — `--brand-50` with `--brand-ink` text.
guidance.Variants and sizes: None. Disabled items (`disabled`) are `--ink-4` and can't be chosen.
guidance.States:
| State | Change |
|---|---|
| Hover | `--surface-2`; nested rows also turn `--brand` |
| Expanded | Chevron rotates 90°, children fade up |
| Current | See Anatomy 4 |
| Disabled | `--ink-4`, not-allowed cursor |
guidance.Accessibility:
- `role="tree"` / `treeitem` / `group`, with `aria-expanded` on rows with children and `aria-selected` + `aria-current` on the current row.
- Keyboard: ↑/↓ move between visible rows, → expands, ← collapses or moves to the parent, Home/End go to the first/last row; Enter/Space activate.
- Name it with `ariaLabel` ("Report folders").
guidance.Do and don't:
| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Show counts on folders | Counts on every nested item |
| Expand the current folder's group by default (`defaultExpanded`) | Open every group at once |
| Keep labels short; they truncate with an ellipsis | Long paths as labels |
guidance.Example:
```tsx
import { Card, Tree } from '@lepide/ds-react';

<Card title="Folders" className="folders">
  <Tree ariaLabel="Report folders" value={folder} onSelect={(f) => setFolder(f.id)} defaultExpanded={['fav']} items={[
    { id: 'all', label: 'All reports', count: 14 },
    { id: 'ad', label: 'Active Directory', count: 4 },
    { id: 'fs', label: 'File server', count: 6 },
    { id: 'fav', label: 'Favourites', count: 2, children: [
      { id: 'r1', label: 'User account lockouts' },
      { id: 'r2', label: 'Permission changes' },
    ] },
  ]} />
</Card>
```

components.title: VerticalTabs
components.summary: A vertical list of section buttons for the left column of settings-style dialogs; the current section gets the selected finish.

exports.name: VerticalTabs
exports.description: Vertical tabs used inside settings-style dialogs (03 § 6). An ARIA tablist: ↑/↓ (and ←/→), Home/End move and select.

props.name: items
props.type: { value: string; label: string; icon?: "settings" | "chevron" | "arrow" | "plus" | "search" | "calendar" | "refresh" | "external" | "share" | "up" | "down" | "eye" | "folder" | "file" | "filter" | "download" | "user" | "logout" | "collapse" | "chevron-right" | "chevrons-left" | "chevrons-right" | "check" | "x" | "minus" | "sort" | "trash" | "chevron-left" | "lock" | "sparkles" | "star" | "bell" | "users" | "clipboard" | "home" | "mail" | "file-search" | "edit" | "more" | "info" | "alert" | "upload" | "server" | "database" | "globe" | "key" | "shield" | "clock" | "play" | "pause" | "link" | "copy" | "layers" | "archive" | "list" | "sliders" | "plug" | "card" | "history" | "restore" | "send" | "terminal" | "cpu" | "tag" | "cloud" | "building" | "user_plus" | "save" | "grid" | undefined; }[]

guidance.When to use:
- The section list inside a settings-style `Modal`, beside the content pane ("General · Schedule · Recipients · Permissions").
- Four or more sections whose labels are too long or too many for `Segmented`.
guidance.When not to use:
- Two to five short sibling views in a page: use `Segmented`.
- Page-level navigation or the settings page section nav: use the sidebar / settings nav.
- Ordered steps the user must complete in sequence: use `Steps` or `WizardCard`.
guidance.Anatomy:
1. Container: `<div class="tabs" role="tablist" aria-orientation="vertical">`, a flex column with a 2 px gap.
2. Item: a `<button>`, 40 px tall, padding 0 12, radius 14 (`--r-md`), 600 13/1 text in `--ink-3`, left-aligned, 10 px gap.
3. Optional leading icon (`icon`): the component passes size 15, and the CSS renders it at 16 × 16.
4. Current item: the selected finish — `--sel-fill`, white text, `--sel-shadow`.

Pair it with a content pane: `.tabs__pane` is a flex column with a 16 px gap that fades up when it mounts (give it a `key` per tab to replay the fade). Lay the two out side by side yourself, for example a grid with a 200 px first column.
guidance.Variants and sizes:
None.

At 620 px and below the list turns into a horizontal row that scrolls sideways (`overflow-x: auto`).
guidance.States:
| State | Change |
|---|---|
| Rest | `--ink-3` text, no fill |
| Hover | `--surface-2` fill, `--ink` text |
| Current | `aria-selected="true"`: `--sel-fill`, white text, `--sel-shadow` |
| Focus | 2 px brand outline (`--focus-outline`), offset 2 px |
guidance.Accessibility:
- An ARIA tablist (`role="tablist"`, `aria-orientation="vertical"`, named by `ariaLabel`): each item is `role="tab"` with `aria-selected`; only the current tab is in the tab order. ↑/↓ (and ←/→) select the previous/next tab, Home/End the first/last, and focus follows. Give the panel `role="tabpanel"` if you need the full pattern.
- `Tab` enters the list on the current tab and leaves it on the next control.
- Move focus or announce the change in the pane only if your content needs it; the component does not.
guidance.Do and don't:
| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Short noun labels: "Schedule", "Recipients" | Verbs or sentences as tab labels |
| Use icons on every item or on none | Mix items with and without icons |
| Keep the dialog's footer actions outside the pane | Put a save button inside each section |
| Use it inside dialogs and narrow side columns | Use it for top-level page navigation |

```tsx import { Modal, VerticalTabs, TextField } from '@lepide/ds-react'; const [tab, setTab] = useState('general');
{tab === 'general' && }
``` Plain HTML (with `@lepide/ds-css`): ```html
```

components.title: Wizard card
components.summary: Full-page multi-step form — a step indicator above a card holding one step's fields, with Back, Cancel and Next/Finish in the footer.

exports.name: WizardCard
exports.description: Full-page wizard card (04 § 10): step indicator, one step body, Back · Cancel · Next/Finish.

guidance.When to use:
- Creating something that needs several screens of settings in a fixed order: a new report, an alert rule, a data-source connection, a scheduled export.
- When each step is a full form (several fields, a table, a picker) that would not fit comfortably in a `Modal`.
guidance.When not to use:
- One screen of fields: use a page form or a `Modal`.
- 2–3 short steps: a `Modal` with `steps` keeps the user on the current page.
- Steps that can be done in any order: use tabs (`VerticalTabs`, `Segmented`) or sections on one settings page.
guidance.Anatomy:
`WizardCard` renders two siblings, so place it in a page column (it has no outer wrapper):
1. Step indicator: `Steps` with `page` (`.steps.steps--page`: no margin, wraps onto lines). 24 px numbered circles (`--surface-3`, 700 11.5 `--ink-3`), 600 13/16 labels in `--ink-4`. The current step uses the selected finish (`--sel-fill`, `--sel-ring`, white number) and an ink label; done steps use the selected finish with a 12 px check and an `--ink-2` label. 2 px connector lines, brand once reached, `--border` otherwise. Leave a gap between it and the card in your layout (e.g. a 16 px flex/grid gap).
2. Card `<section class="lf-card wiz-card page-form">`: white, radius 20, no padding, overflow hidden. `.page-form` styles every `Field`/`TextField` inside: 46 px inputs on `--surface-2`, radius 14, white with the brand `--ring` on focus, red border and a shake when invalid.
3. Body `.wiz-card__body`: padding 24, flex column, gap 16 — the current step's `children`.
4. Footer `.wiz-card__foot`: padding 16 24, top hairline `--border-soft`, `--surface-2` fill, 8 px gap. Left: Back (secondary, `chevron-left` icon, hidden on the first step), then `extraFooter`. A `.spacer` pushes the rest right: Cancel (secondary), then the primary Next button with a trailing `arrow` icon. On the last step the primary reads `finishLabel` (default "Finish") and has no icon.
guidance.Variants and sizes: None.
guidance.States:
| State | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| First step (`step === 0`) | No Back button |
| Middle step | Back, Cancel, Next (`nextLabel` or "Next") with a trailing arrow |
| Last step (`step === steps.length - 1`) | Primary reads `finishLabel` ("Finish" by default), no arrow |
| `busy` | The primary button shows a spinner, is disabled and has `aria-busy="true"` (Back and Cancel stay enabled — disable them yourself if needed) |
| `onStep` passed | Done steps in the indicator become clickable (pointer, `role="button"`, Enter or Space) and call `onStep(index)`; current and future steps are not clickable |

`WizardCard` holds no state: you own `step`, validate in `onNext` before advancing, and decide what Cancel does (usually confirm if anything was entered, then navigate away).
guidance.Accessibility:
- The indicator is an `<ol aria-label="Progress">`; the current step has `aria-current="step"`. Step labels are React keys, so they must be unique.
- All footer controls are real `<button>`s in reading order: Back, extra, Cancel, Next/Finish.
- When the step changes, move focus to the step's first field or heading (the card does not do this for you), so keyboard and screen-reader users start at the new content.
- Show validation errors on the fields (`Field` `error`, which renders `role="alert"`) rather than only disabling Next.
guidance.Do and don't:
| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Short noun step labels: "Source", "Columns", "Schedule", "Review" | Sentences or numbered labels ("Step 1: Choose…") |
| Finish with a verb that says what happens: `finishLabel="Create alert"` | Leave "Finish" when a clearer verb exists |
| Validate the step in `onNext`; keep Next enabled and explain what's missing | Disable Next with no explanation |
| Let users go back with `onStep` and Back without losing input | Reset later steps when going back |
